cards.name: MICE as single-imputation ICE, hand-rolled on MissForestImputer's loop (BayesianRidge for numerical targets, multinomial LogisticRegression for categorical ones) [RECOMMENDED for 'MICE (to add)']
cards.availability: No new dependency. scikit-learn 1.9.0 is locked and installed (.venv/Lib/site-packages/sklearn/__init__.py:45; uv.lock:2896-2897), BSD-3. BayesianRidge and LogisticRegression are stable estimators. Unlike IterativeImputer they need no `sklearn.experimental` opt-in, and IterativeImputer is still experimental in 1.9 (.venv/Lib/site-packages/sklearn/experimental/enable_iterative_imputer.py:1-13; https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.impute.IterativeImputer.html, docs for 1.9.1).
cards.api_fit: Implements the BaselineImputer protocol (src/training/imputation_baselines.py:54-69) in a module of its own, e.g. src/training/mice.py. imputation_baselines.py stays byte-identical because its source keys the ADR 0007 cache (src/training/baseline_cache.py:15-18, 64-73). The recipe has three parts, each copied from an existing baseline. (1) The loop from missforest.py:106-178: fit on the training fold; Gauss-Seidel rounds over the columns in ascending-missingness order; every column gets a model whether or not it has gaps (ADR 0016 decision 2, docs/adr/0016-missforest-baselines.md:81-87); the fitted models are replayed on the test rows, so the baseline stays inductive like the model; stopping by still_converging, or a fixed 10 rounds as in IterativeImputer's max_iter. (2) Only `_fit_one` changes (missforest.py:196-225): a BayesianRidge for a numerical target, and a multinomial lbfgs LogisticRegression for a categorical target, predicted as its training-vocabulary index, which is hgb's convention (imputation_baselines.py:273-275, 311-312). The constant fallbacks for an empty, single-valued or feature-less column stay as they are. (3) The design matrix changes for categorical features. A linear model cannot read a vocabulary index as a number; missForest does this (missforest.py:88-89) only because forests tolerate it. Categorical features therefore enter as one-hot blocks over the training vocabulary, as in KnnImputer._matrix (imputation_baselines.py:148-160), and the target's own block is left out of its predictors. Filled categories feed later rounds as hard one-hot. Protocol details stay as they are: cells are hidden by a boolean mask, never by writing NaN into the frame (:11-13); the 'nan', [MASK] and [NULL] markers are excluded from every vocabulary (_NOT_A_CLASS, :33-34); categories come back as as_category_strings strings; numerical columns are already in the frame's scaled space, so no extra scaling is needed. Nothing draws random numbers: BayesianRidge point predictions and lbfgs are deterministic, so ADR 0007 decision 6 (global streams untouched) holds trivially. Wiring: a 4th `_Family` in baseline_cache.py:64-73, plus either the bar or `EXTERNAL_BASELINES` (src/training/summary.py:88-92). Which of the two is the owner's call and needs an ADR, as with 0017. Strict mypy: stubs/sklearn/ has no linear_model, so hand-written stubs for BayesianRidge and LogisticRegression are needed (ADR 0006).
cards.categorical_support: Every categorical column gets a model suited to its type: multinomial logistic regression for credit-g's 13 categoricals (2-10 levels; purpose has 10), kr-vs-kp's 36 (35 binary, katri ternary) and electricity's day (7 levels) (datasets/categorical_columns/*.txt; level counts taken from datasets/datasets_raw/*.csv). Categorical features enter as one-hot. A category the training fold never shows is a gap and can't be answered, the same rule as hgb and KNN. Default L2 (C=1) keeps credit-g's ~50 dummy features stable on 700 training rows. kr-vs-kp is entirely categorical, so on it ICE becomes 36 chained logistic regressions.
cards.feasible_tables: All 9 tables and all 21 variants, CPU only, with no size or memory limit (largest: electricity at 31,717 x 8 training rows, letter at 14,000 x 16). Expect the 10-round cap to be hit at 60-80nan, as missForest hits it (ADR 0016:58-60).
cards.known_failures: (1) Point error, which matters for impute_score. MICE had the worst sample-wise error at every rate in Shadbahr et al. and the best distributional fit by KS and Wasserstein (references/shadbahr-imputation-quality-paper.md:157-159). In CACTI's Table 1, MICE's RMSE (1.06) is worse than Mean's (0.95), with R² 0.19 against MissForest's 0.35 (references/cacti-paper.md:235-239). That MICE is HyperImpute's posterior-sampling plugin, and the sampling is why the fork should run the conditional-mean variant (ICE). (2) On natural health data, Iterative was on par with mean imputation (rank 9.0 vs 7.5) because the features depend on each other only weakly (references/perez-lebel-benchmark-paper.md:144). (3) Self-masking MNAR: an imputer can't see its own mask. Single `mice` imputation misclassified 52-63% of a binary hidden only when it equalled 1 (concepts/missing-data-imputation.md:98, Ehrig). (4) ADR 0007 rejected IterativeImputer as 'linear on a one-hot matrix', stochastic, behind an experimental import and not obviously stronger than KNN (docs/adr/0007-baseline-imputers-scored-on-the-decoders-cells.md:196-198). This design removes the first three objections: one-hot is used only for features, with the own block excluded; nothing is sampled; no experimental import is needed. The fourth probably stands on the nonlinear tables (letter, pendigits, vehicle).
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: None in impute_score units. Spambase and letter appear in ReMasker's benchmark, which has ICE and MICE among its 13 baselines, but it reports min-max RMSE and amputates at most 8 columns, so on Spambase '30%' hides 30% of 8 of the 57 columns (references/remasker-paper.md:132-144). CACTI has Spambase and Letter only inside 10-dataset averages (references/cacti-paper.md:212-213, 238). MFAN has letter, pendigits and spam with MICE (linear regression), but only as downstream accuracy (references/mfan-paper.md:119-131). The sanity check available is relative, against the fork's own E35 bar (docs/adr/0017-missforest-outside-the-bar.md:143-165): ICE should land between mean_mode (1.0) and hgb/lgbm on the nonlinear 20nan tables, and near hgb on spambase and biodeg.
cards.wrapper_effort: About 1 day for live runs only; 1.5-2 days to put it on the E35 table. Breakdown: the imputer class, ~120-170 lines reusing missforest.py's loop, stopping rule and fallbacks, 3-4 h. One-hot design with own-block exclusion, 1-2 h. Unit tests on the fork's existing pattern (complete-fold rule, identical fills at 1 and 8 BLAS threads, global streams untouched, categorical round-trip '1' not '1.0'), 2-3 h. sklearn.linear_model stubs, 0.5 h. Cache family, summary constant and ADR, 1-2 h. A backfill cloned from scripts/backfill_lgbm_baseline.py (387 lines) onto the ~887 imputation parents, 4-6 h plus a dry run on gorgona8, which only the owner can apply because the server writes the store.
cards.compute_estimate: Cheap. Each round fits one linear or logistic model per column: under a second to a few seconds per fold fit for all ≤10 rounds, even on electricity (7-class logistic on 31.7k rows) and spambase (57 BayesianRidges per round on 3.2k rows). missForest's measured 9-57 s per fold fit (docs/adr/0016-missforest-baselines.md:44-56) is a loose upper bound; expect at least 10x less. 21 variants x 15 fold pairs = 315 fits, scored on 2 populations: under 1 CPU-hour, no GPU. A backfill's wall time would be dominated by MLflow I/O and the cache recomputing the other families; ADR 0017's backfill over 887 parents took about 2 h (docs/adr/0017-missforest-outside-the-bar.md:119-124). BLAS may change last digits across machines; the cache already keys on the hostname (baseline_cache.py:9-13, 77-83).
cards.gap_exposed: (a) The fork has no parametric or linear conditional imputer. Every learned baseline is KNN or trees, while the thesis plan lists 'MICE (to add)' (projects/trident/thesis-goals.md:141) and a reviewer expects the classical row. (b) Untested hypothesis that bears on t1: at 60-80nan the bar is mean_mode at 1.000, and every learned baseline scores above 1.0 (lgbm 1.043-1.112, missForest 1.021-1.093), with the model at 0.976-1.008 (docs/adr/0017-missforest-outside-the-bar.md:149-150, 157, 163). A shrinkage-regularised linear ICE falls back toward the mean instead of overshooting it, so it may land just below 1.0. It would then set the bar exactly where t1 looks, and if it joins the bar it could change the model's verdict on credit-g_60/80nan, kr-vs-kp_80nan and spambase_80nan. (c) impute_score is a per-cell point error, so it can't credit MICE's documented strengths: distributional fidelity (Shadbahr) and multiple-imputation coverage (MaCoDE 0.944-0.963 vs MICE 0.79-0.88; concepts/missing-data-imputation.md:88). That calls for a distributional or coverage metric beside impute_score before any MNAR-bias claim (RQ3).
cards.rq_or_todo: thesis-goals Baselines 'MICE (to add)' (projects/trident/thesis-goals.md:141); an RQ1 imputation baseline; the imputation-side half of t1 at 60/80nan (_meta/todos.md:19). Its imputer is the transform the classification-side card reuses for t1/t3 and RQ2's 'conditional imputation +/- indicator' arms (thesis-goals.md:150).
cards.reasons: It is the only variant that handles credit-g, kr-vs-kp and electricity the way hgb, lgbm, KNN and missForest already do (vocabulary-index targets, one-hot features for a linear learner, an inductive fit replayed on the test rows), and it adds no dependency or randomness. The code is about a day, built from three existing pieces. Bringing it to MEDIUM: the strict-mypy stubs, a 4th cache family, a bar-or-external ADR decision, and a backfill if it is to appear on the E35 table. It is QUICK if logged only on new live runs as an external baseline. Use the name 'ice' (conditional mean) for the imputation task: impute_score rewards point estimates, and posterior draws only add noise (CACTI's MICE row is worse than Mean).

cards.name: scikit-learn IterativeImputer as a drop-in (BayesianRidge default; ExtraTrees/RandomForest estimator variants)
cards.availability: In the locked scikit-learn 1.9.0 (.venv/Lib/site-packages/sklearn/impute/_iterative.py:314-333), BSD-3, but still experimental: `from sklearn.experimental import enable_iterative_imputer` is required (enable_iterative_imputer.py:1-13), and the 1.9.1 docs say the API and predictions may change without deprecation. The fork's hand-written stubs (stubs/sklearn/impute/__init__.pyi) cover only KNNImputer.
cards.api_fit: The inductive shape fits: `fit` on the training-fold matrix, `transform` on the test matrix with hidden cells set to NaN, wrapped as KnnImputer is (imputation_baselines.py:129-177), with `keep_empty_features=True` so column positions don't shift (:142-146). The default `skip_complete=False` gives complete columns a model. With `sample_posterior=False`, default order and `n_nearest_features=None`, `random_state` is unused and the fill is deterministic. The ExtraTrees and RandomForest variants are just missForest again: the fork already has a better-specified missForest (R defaults, R stopping rule), ADR 0016:98-104. The blocker is that one estimator serves every column, so categoricals must become numbers, and both encodings fail (see categorical_support).
cards.categorical_support: Numeric-only, and both workarounds are flawed. (i) Vocabulary indices as numbers, rounded and clipped through min_value/max_value: a linear regression on nominal codes, the reason ADR 0016 rejected missForest-through-IterativeImputer (docs/adr/0016-missforest-baselines.md:209-210). For kr-vs-kp's 35 binary columns this is a tolerable linear probability model. For credit-g purpose (10 levels) and electricity day (7) it imposes an arbitrary order. (ii) One-hot blocks as in KNN, my own reasoning, untested: on observed rows each dummy equals 1 minus its siblings, so its BayesianRidge learns that identity. In a hidden row every sibling starts at its training frequency, so the dummy is predicted back at its frequency, and the chain never leaves the initial fill: argmax returns the training mode, i.e. the mean_mode baseline on every categorical cell. IterativeImputer can't exclude a target's own block from its predictors; it can only subsample randomly through n_nearest_features.
cards.feasible_tables: Clean only on the 6 numeric-only tables, 15 of 21 variants: spambase x4, vehicle x2, biodeg x2, kc2 x2, pendigits, letter. Wrong or degenerate categorical fills on credit-g x4, kr-vs-kp x4 and electricity (6 variants).
cards.known_failures: Same as the ICE card, plus the experimental API. HyperImpute's 'mice' plugin is exactly this estimator with sample_posterior=True averaged over draws (n_imputations defaults to 1 in code), and that is CACTI's 'MICE' row, with RMSE worse than Mean (references/cacti-paper.md:238-239). Rockenschaub used ICE (BayesianRidge conditional mean, 10 iterations) and MICE (posterior sampling, 5 draws averaged) (references/rockenschaub-missingness-shift-paper.md:90-91).
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: none found in comparable units (see the ICE card: ReMasker and CACTI include spambase and letter only in min-max RMSE or averaged form)
cards.wrapper_effort: 2-3 h for a numeric-only wrapper with stubs. Its best use is as a test oracle: on the 6 numeric-only tables, with the same order and rounds, the hand-rolled ICE should reproduce IterativeImputer's fills closely, which is a cheap correctness check for the recommended card. Making it handle categoricals properly turns it into the hand-rolled ICE.
cards.compute_estimate: Seconds per fold; 315 fold fits under 1 CPU-hour.
cards.gap_exposed: The protocol's mixed-type tables are where the off-the-shelf MICE fails. Any thesis row labelled 'MICE (IterativeImputer)' on credit-g, kr-vs-kp or electricity would actually be a numeric-coded or mode-collapsed imputer, so the categorical encoding must be stated in the methods.
cards.rq_or_todo: thesis-goals.md:141 (not sufficient on its own); a test oracle for the ICE card.
cards.reasons: Quick only for the 15 numeric-only variants. On the 6 mixed variants it either regresses nominal codes (already rejected in ADR 0016) or, one-hot, collapses to the mode. It also brings back ADR 0007's experimental-import objection. Not recommended as the thesis's MICE; useful as an oracle.

cards.name: miceforest (LightGBM-based MICE with predictive mean matching)
cards.availability: PyPI miceforest 6.0.5, uploaded 2025-10-27 (6.0.4 the day before; 6.0.1-6.0.3 in July-August 2024). MIT, Python >=3.10. Requires lightgbm>=4.1.0 (4.7.0 locked), pandas>=2.1.0 (2.3.3), pyarrow>=6.0.1 (23.0.1 locked under the pyproject's pyarrow<24), scipy>=1.6 (1.17.1/1.18.0 locked) and numpy, so it likely installs without moving other locked versions (inferred, not tried). Repo https://github.com/AnotherSamWilson/miceforest: 413 stars, 11 open issues, 1 open PR. https://pypi.org/pypi/miceforest/json
cards.api_fit: `ImputationKernel(data: DataFrame, num_datasets=1, variable_schema=None, imputation_order='ascending', mean_match_candidates=5, mean_match_strategy='normal', save_all_iterations_data=True, random_state=None)`, then `kernel.mice(iterations, **lgb_params)`, then `kernel.impute_new_data(new_data, ...)` for an inductive fill (https://miceforest.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ImputationKernel.html). What the wrapper must do: (1) build a DataFrame copy with hidden cells set to NaN, categoricals as pandas `category` dtype over the fixed training vocabulary, so the '1.0' stringify hazard (imputation_baselines.py:11-13) never arises; (2) pass `variable_schema` covering every column, because with None it trains models only for columns with training gaps, so a test-fold-only hidden column would get none (ADR 0016's departure 2); (3) keep the training data in the kernel (`save_all_iterations_data=True`), since impute_new_data draws mean-matching candidates from it; (4) set `mean_match_candidates=0` for point predictions; (5) pass LightGBM's deterministic=True, force_row_wise=True and a thread count through the mice kwargs, as the lgbm baseline does (lightgbm_baseline.py:52-58), and seed `random_state`, then verify the global streams stay untouched (ADR 0007 decision 6).
cards.categorical_support: Native: pandas category dtype, LightGBM categorical splits, and a 'fast' mean-matching strategy for binary and categorical columns that samples a class from the predicted probabilities, which makes it stochastic.
cards.feasible_tables: All 21 variants. The LightGBM default of at least 20 rows per leaf starves the small tables (kc2: 364 training rows; credit-g at 60-80nan), as ADR 0016 measured for its LightGBM missForest (docs/adr/0016-missforest-baselines.md:185-189).
cards.known_failures: With mean matching off, miceforest is essentially ADR 0016's `missforest_lgbm`, which ADR 0016 itself called 'in the spirit of miceforest, without that package's multiple imputation or mean matching' (docs/adr/0016-missforest-baselines.md:105-107). It scored below the forest on every variant of both populations, never set the bar, and was withdrawn (docs/adr/0017-missforest-outside-the-bar.md:21-23, 53-55, 101-102). With mean matching on (the default, 5 candidates), donor draws add noise to a point-error metric. The docs are inconsistent: `imputation_order` lists 'latin' in the signature but 'roman'/'arabic' in the text, and `variable_schema`'s typing differs between signature and text.
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: none found
cards.wrapper_effort: 6-10 h: wrapper, dtype round-trip and schema, determinism and global-stream tests, a new dependency in pyproject and uv.lock (an `uv sync` on Windows), an ADR, then a cache family and a backfill as in the ICE card.
cards.compute_estimate: About ADR 0016's missforest_lgbm: 1.8-59 s per fold fit, 0.0-0.4 s per fill (docs/adr/0016-missforest-baselines.md:44-56). Times num_datasets for multiple imputation.
cards.gap_exposed: None beyond what the fork already measured: an iterated LightGBM per column is already known to be weaker than missForest here. Its distinct value is genuine multiple imputation with mean matching on mixed types, which matters for the classification-side MI arm or a coverage metric, not for impute_score.
cards.rq_or_todo: Possibly the MI generator for t1/t3's multiple-imputation arm (_meta/todos.md:19, 21) or for an RQ3 coverage analysis; not the thesis's 'MICE (to add)'.
cards.reasons: Feasible and maintained (released October 2025, MIT, compatible with the locked lightgbm, pandas and pyarrow), with native categoricals. But as a point imputer it duplicates a baseline the owner withdrew, and its default mean matching is stochastic and needs the training data kept. Not the pick for impute_score; keep it in reserve for multiple imputation on the classification folds.
evidence: https://miceforest.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ImputationKernel.html (constructor and impute_new_data signatures; training data needed)

cards.name: HyperImpute 'mice' / 'ice' plugins
cards.availability: PyPI hyperimpute 0.1.17, last released 2023-02-28, MIT. A heavy dependency tree: torch, catboost, xgboost, optuna, loguru==0.6.0, miracle-imputation, geomloss, redis, jupyter, notebook (https://pypi.org/pypi/hyperimpute/json). Repo https://github.com/vanderschaarlab/hyperimpute.
cards.api_fit: Poor; the fork already smoke-tested it on gorgona8 (docs/adr/0016-missforest-baselines.md:200-205). It breaks on scikit-learn 1.9 (`LogisticRegression(multi_class=...)` was removed) unless logistic regression leaves its search space; it moves the global random streams; its `fit` does nothing and its `transform` fits on the frame it fills, which makes it transductive on the test fold; it took 47 s per credit-g fold on 200 rows. Plugin internals: 'mice' is sklearn IterativeImputer with its BayesianRidge default, sample_posterior=True, one imputer per n_imputations (1 in code, though the docstring says 5), the draws averaged, max_iter=100, tol=1e-3, seeds random_state+idx (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vanderschaarlab/hyperimpute/main/src/hyperimpute/plugins/imputers/plugin_mice.py). 'ice' is HyperImpute's own engine with fixed linear_regression/logistic_regression seeds and class_threshold=5 (plugin_ice.py), and its logistic half is exactly the piece that breaks on sklearn 1.9.
cards.categorical_support: 'mice': numeric only, categories as numbers. 'ice': columns with at most 5 unique values are treated as classes and fit with logistic regression, which fails on the locked sklearn 1.9.
cards.feasible_tables: None as-is under the protocol (sklearn incompatibility and transductive fit).
cards.known_failures: See ADR 0016:200-205. CACTI notes HyperImpute can't impute out of sample (references/cacti-paper.md:203). The 'mice' plugin's posterior sampling makes CACTI's MICE row worse than Mean on RMSE (references/cacti-paper.md:238-239).
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: ReMasker's ICE and MICE baselines (spambase, letter) were run 'at their defaults' (references/remasker-paper.md:138), probably through these plugins (inferred), in min-max RMSE with at most 8 columns amputated; not comparable to impute_score.
cards.wrapper_effort: Not worth it. Both plugins can be reproduced directly from sklearn ('mice' = IterativeImputer with sample_posterior and averaging; 'ice' = the hand-rolled ICE card) with no new dependency.
cards.compute_estimate: 47 s per credit-g fold on 200 rows, from the fork's smoke test (ADR 0016:205).
cards.gap_exposed: None new.
cards.rq_or_todo: None; cite it only to explain what the literature's 'ICE'/'MICE' rows are.
cards.reasons: Unmaintained since February 2023, already found broken on the fork's scikit-learn 1.9, transductive, touches global RNG streams, and pulls GPU-heavy dependencies; both plugins are trivial to reproduce without it.

cards.name: MICE/ICE + missing indicator as a classification preprocessor (t1, t3, step zero)
cards.availability: Imputer: the ICE card's module reused as a fold-fitted transform, or for numeric-only tables sklearn IterativeImputer(add_indicator=True). Multiple imputation: m posterior draws (BayesianRidge with sample_posterior) or miceforest num_datasets. No classification pipeline exists in the fork: every experiment from E01 to E39 is on the imputation task.
cards.api_fit: Not the BaselineImputer protocol. It is a preprocessing step inside classification folds that don't exist yet: fit the imputer on the training split only, transform validation and test, append the 0/1 indicators, then train XGBoost, LightGBM or an MLP. It also feeds TRIDENT's RQ2 encoding arms: 'missForest or condexp + indicator' and 'conditional imputation without an indicator' (projects/trident/thesis-goals.md:150). Never use y in the imputation model at prediction time; Rockenschaub refits the imputer without Y (references/rockenschaub-missingness-shift-paper.md:92). For MI, train m classifiers and pool their outputs, as Shadbahr did following van Buuren (references/shadbahr-imputation-quality-paper.md:99).
cards.categorical_support: As in the ICE card (multinomial logistic for categorical targets, one-hot features); the indicator is per column.
cards.feasible_tables: All 9 tables once classification folds exist; t1 targets 60-80% (credit-g, kr-vs-kp, spambase are the only tables with 60/80nan variants).
cards.known_failures: On natural health data, Iterative+mask was on par with Mean+mask, and bagging, not the conditional imputer, drove the multiple-imputation gain (references/perez-lebel-benchmark-paper.md:138-145). Under self-masking MNAR, imputing better can lower downstream performance without an indicator (projects/trident/thesis-goals.md:66). TRIDENT's own Table 3 was tuned on test macro-F1, so the comparison needs validation-based retuning first (thesis-goals.md:152, step zero).
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: TRIDENT paper Table 3 has no MICE row: its baselines are XGBoost, LightGBM, RF, TabNet, FT-Transformer and SAINT via TabZilla, one split, seed 42. None found.
cards.wrapper_effort: The imputer itself adds about 2 h on top of the ICE card. Everything else is the step-zero classification pipeline (folds, classifiers, seeds, validation HPO, macro-F1 paired CIs), several days of work not specific to MICE.
cards.compute_estimate: Imputation is negligible (seconds per fold). The cost is classifiers x m imputations x ≥5 seeds x 5 folds x tables, plus TRIDENT's GPU fine-tuning, and it all depends on step zero.
cards.gap_exposed: t1 is a classification question ('does TRIDENT's macro-F1 advantage at 60–80% survive against missForest/MICE + missing-indicator inputs', synthesis/missing-data-imputation-x-null-token-embeddings.md:79). The fork's imputation results can't answer it, and the fork has no classification number at all.
cards.rq_or_todo: t1 (_meta/todos.md:19), t3 (_meta/todos.md:21), step zero (projects/trident/thesis-goals.md:152), RQ2 arms (thesis-goals.md:150).
cards.reasons: MICE itself is cheap here, but the work is blocked on the classification pipeline the fork lacks (step zero). For t1, the best variant is the ICE card's conditional-mean imputer plus a per-column indicator as the primary arm, the literature's 'Iterative+mask' or 'ICE + mask', with m=5 posterior-draw MICE pooled over classifiers as a secondary arm; both reuse one module.

cards.name: HyperImpute (vanderschaarlab/hyperimpute, ICML 2022) as a source of extra imputation baselines: hyperimpute AutoML, GAIN, MIWAE, Sinkhorn, SoftImpute (plus mice/ice/EM/missforest/miracle/mean/median/most_frequent/nop)

The repo is not archived but has gone quiet: last push 2023-04-04, 202 stars, and 4 open issues from 2023-10 to 2025-04 with no maintainer reply (https://github.com/vanderschaarlab/hyperimpute/issues). Fork env, checked read-only: Python 3.11.15, torch 2.5.1+cu121 (CUDA available), numpy 2.4.6, pandas 2.3.3, scikit-learn 1.9.0, pydantic 2.13.4, lightgbm 4.7.0. Installed already: cloudpickle. Not installed: hyperimpute, xgboost, catboost, geomloss, loguru, tensorflow, redis. Plugins load lazily, and a failed import is only logged (core/base_plugin.py PluginLoader._load_single_plugin catches BaseException). So `uv pip install --no-deps hyperimpute==0.1.17 geomloss loguru==0.6.0 xgboost catboost`, without TF or jupyter, gives every plugin except miracle. With `uv add`, the lock (both machines) would pull TF and jupyter unless a uv `override-dependencies` entry neutralises miracle-imputation.
cards.api_fit: Target protocol: `BaselineImputer` with `name`, `fit(train_frame)` and `impute(frame, hidden)`. impute returns every hidden-or-NaN cell filled: numerical columns as floats in the fork's scaled space, categorical columns as `as_category_strings` labels, in the frame's column order (src/training/imputation_baselines.py:54-69). A family plugs in like missForest and lgbm: a module with `fit_<x>_imputers(train, num_cols, cat_cols) -> list[BaselineImputer]` (missforest.py:262-270, lightgbm_baseline.py:64-72), a `_Family(name, source modules, library names, fit)` entry in baseline_cache.py:64-74 (the library versions enter the cache key, :77), and a listing in summary.EXTERNAL_BASELINES (summary.py:88) so it stays outside the bar the way ADR 0017 keeps missForest out. The wrapper has to do six things. (1) Encode the frame as a float matrix. Numerical columns go in as they are. Categorical columns become a one-hot block over the training fold's vocabulary minus `_NOT_A_CLASS` ("nan", [MASK], [NULL]; imputation_baselines.py:34), with NaN where a cell is hidden, missing or a category the fold never shows: KnnImputer._matrix, :148-160. Decode a block by argmax (:171-176). For the AutoML plugin, use hgb-style ordinal codes instead (:277-293). (2) Split by fit semantics. Inductive, i.e. fit on train and transform on test, works for MIWAE (plugin_miwae _fit trains, _transform imputes), mice/ice/sklearn_* and GAIN, but only through the inner `GainImputation` class, which has real fit/transform. The GainPlugin itself refits on whatever it is asked to transform (plugin_gain.py:369-371). Transductive, where `_fit` is a no-op and `_transform` re-runs the whole method on the frame it gets: hyperimpute (plugin_hyperimpute.py:124-128), sinkhorn (plugin_sinkhorn.py:194-195), EM (plugin_EM.py:244), miracle; softimpute's fit only cross-validates the shrinkage. The wiki agrees: "HyperImpute and Sinkhorn can't impute out of sample" (references/cacti-paper.md:203). For these, keep the training matrix in fit(), stack train rows over test rows (hidden cells set to NaN) in impute(), run fit_transform and slice out the test rows. Every scored population (induced, masked) then costs a full fit, and the method sees all test rows' visible cells together, while TRIDENT decodes one row at a time. That protocol difference has to be stated. (3) Bypass the plugins' hyperparameter bugs. GainPlugin builds `GainImputation()` with no arguments (plugin_gain.py:349; issue #42), and SoftImputePlugin builds `SoftImpute(random_state)` with no arguments (plugin_softimpute.py:298). Both silently ignore every hyperparameter passed in, so instantiate the inner classes directly. MIWAE's defaults are latent_size=1 and n_hidden=1 (plugin_miwae.py:58-59), so pass real sizes. (4) HyperImpute AutoML: pass `classifier_seed` without `logistic_regression`. That plugin calls LogisticRegression(multi_class=...), a parameter scikit-learn 1.9 no longer has (checked: False), and the model is built outside the try in `_eval_params` (_hyperimpute_internals.py:174), so any column the plugin treats as categorical crashes the whole run. Also override `model._is_categorical` with the fork's own column lists; columns are str-mapped in _setup. (5) RNG isolation. Every plugin `__init__` calls `enable_reproducible_results`, which reseeds the global numpy, torch and random streams (imputers/base.py:31; utils/distributions.py), and GAIN, MIWAE, Sinkhorn and pandas `.sample` (_internals.py:782) all draw from those global streams. The fork forbids touching the global streams (imputation_baselines.py:40-43; docs/BACKLOG.md:370ff, I3). So save and restore the numpy/random/torch CPU and CUDA states around construct, fit and impute, or run the family only from a backfill. (6) Keep the family out of live runs. BaselineScorer scores every family by default (baseline_cache.py:96), so an HyperImpute fit would otherwise run inside every training run.
cards.categorical_support: The HyperImpute AutoML plugin alone separates categorical columns, and only by a heuristic: a column with fewer than class_threshold=5 unique values, NaN included, gets LabelEncoder plus a classifier (plugin_hyperimpute.py:66; _hyperimpute_internals.py:860-862, 679-702). Every other column is regressed, an object column on its label codes. Without an override, credit-g columns such as purpose (about 10 levels) and electricity's day (7) would be imputed by regression on codes, while numeric columns with fewer than 5 distinct values would be classified. GAIN, MIWAE, Sinkhorn, SoftImpute and EM are numeric-only, so the wrapper one-hot encodes and decodes by argmax. GAIN's sigmoid output and MIWAE's Student-t likelihood treat one-hot blocks as continuous, an approximation. ReMasker and CACTI fed scaled codes instead, and BACKLOG I3 notes that one-hot blocks would be a departure that has to be stated. Only credit-g, kr-vs-kp and electricity are affected. kr-vs-kp is all binary or ternary, so without the logistic_regression fix the AutoML plugin crashes on every column there.
cards.feasible_tables: In memory terms all 21 variants fit on CPU. The largest union is electricity, about 45k rows × 8 columns plus a 7-level one-hot; spambase is the widest at 57 columns. The constraints are practical, not hard limits. (a) SoftImpute's default max_rank=2 is not a fair setting on wide tables (spambase 57, kr-vs-kp 36, biodeg 41), so the rank has to be chosen and documented. (b) At 60/80nan (credit-g, kr-vs-kp, spambase), GAIN and MIWAE are known to degrade, and the AutoML plugin is slowest on spambase, which has the most columns times iterations. (c) Sinkhorn is pinned to CPU: core/device.py sets DEVICE = "cpu" (issue #43). The batch is fixed at 512 (2^floor(log2(n/2)) on kc2), so cost grows with the number of iterations, not rows, and all 21 variants are feasible. GPU only by monkeypatching the module global. (d) Run MIWAE on CPU (issue #44, a zero encoder scale on CUDA). All 21 variants are feasible for all five methods. Spambase ×4 and electricity/letter dominate HyperImpute's cost.
cards.known_failures: From code and issues: GainPlugin ignores its own hyperparameters (#42, open since 2024-05; plugin_gain.py:349). SoftImputePlugin does the same (plugin_softimpute.py:298). MIWAE defaults to a 1-unit, 1-latent network with an empty hyperparameter space, and crashes on a zero Normal scale (#44, the proposed fix being +0.001 on the encoder scale at plugin_miwae.py:89/138). Benchmarks that ran "at their defaults" through this library, as ReMasker did with 13 baselines (wiki references/remasker-paper.md:138), therefore report a degenerate MIWAE and a GAIN with untuned defaults; that is my inference, not stated in those papers. On the fork's scikit-learn 1.9, the logistic_regression prediction plugin raises TypeError and takes the AutoML imputer down with it. Pydantic v1 `validate_arguments` still imports on 2.13.4 (checked). numpy functions applied to torch tensors still work on numpy 2.4.6, with an `__array_wrap__` DeprecationWarning (checked). `X[col][mask] = np.clip(...)` (_internals.py:838) is chained assignment and would silently do nothing under pandas Copy-on-Write or pandas 3. Candidate-model failures inside the AutoML search are swallowed as failure_score (_internals.py:176-187), so a broken learner disappears without an error. From the wiki: Grzesiak et al. 2025 (arXiv 2511.04833; _raw/litreview-2026-10/D-benchmarks-theory.md:462-463) rank mice_cart > aregImpute > mice_rf > hyperimpute on numerical data and find that deep methods (MIWAE, GAIN, MIRACLE, ReMasker) "consistently underperform". PMAE reports HyperImpute losing 21 points from Monotone to General patterns (skills/missingness-robustness-benchmark.md:146). HyperImpute's built-in forests are small, 10 trees of depth 4 (references/imputation-for-prediction-paper.md:107). The library's "MNAR" generator comes in two different variants across papers (concepts/missingness-mechanisms.md:132).
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: Only letter and spambase overlap. The paper's Table 4 lists 12 UCI sets, including letter (20000×16) and spam (4601×57); there is no credit-g, kr-vs-kp, vehicle, biodeg, kc2, pendigits or electricity. The repo's "credit" is UCI credit-screening crx (690 rows), not credit-g. Numbers: letter, MAR 30%, min-max scaled, in-sample, RMSE ×10 (paper Tables 2/6, arXiv 2206.07769): HyperImpute 0.524±0.067, ice_lr 1.087±0.149, ice_rf 1.118±0.148, ice_cb 0.750±0.099, so HyperImpute's RMSE is about 0.48× that of linear ICE. ReMasker Table 5 gives HyperImpute an RMSE of 0.0564 on letter under the same protocol (wiki references/remasker-paper.md:180), consistent with the paper. Spambase appears only as bars in the paper's Figure 2, with no table. CACTI's Table 1 averages over 10 datasets, Spambase and Letter included, with in-sample RMSE under MCAR: HyperImpute 0.72, missForest 0.77, Mean 0.95. That is roughly 0.76× mean and 0.94× missForest (wiki references/cacti-paper.md:234), a loose expected range for impute_score. Caveats: MAR rather than MCAR, min-max scaling, in-sample fit_transform, RMSE rather than error/mean-mode. The repo notebooks' letter drops the last column (yegvx) as y and keeps the letter label as a feature, and they read spambase without header=None, losing one row (experiments_01 notebook cells 44, 47). These numbers are a sanity check of direction only, not targets.
cards.wrapper_effort: About 4-6 h for a dry-run-quality wrapper of GAIN (inner class, inductive), MIWAE (plugin with sizes set and the scale fix, CPU), SoftImpute (inner class, stacked) and Sinkhorn (plugin, stacked). That covers the shared encode/decode adapter reused from KnnImputer._matrix, the stack-and-slice helper, the RNG save/restore context, the _Family entry and a one-fold smoke test on kc2_20nan. HyperImpute AutoML adds about 2 h: the seed list without LR, the `_is_categorical` override, and a check that `_tear_down` returns the codes. Bringing it up to the fork's standard, the way ADR 0016/0017 did for missForest and lgbm, takes another 6-8 h: an ADR, unit tests like test_lightgbm_baseline.py (137 lines) and test_missforest.py (235 lines), a backfill script like scripts/backfill_lgbm_baseline.py (387 lines, dry run by default; writes go to gorgona8's store), and the EXTERNAL_BASELINES and gap_to_* plumbing in summary.py. Total: about a working day to see numbers, about 2 days to land it properly. Install: 0.5-1 h on each of two machines, longer if uv.lock has to carry it.
cards.compute_estimate: Folds are seeded (src/training/data.py:218-221, KFold(random_state=seed)), so there are 21 × 15 = 315 training folds and, with two populations, 630 scorings. GAIN (1000 steps, batch 256): about 5-10 s per fit, about 1 h in total. SoftImpute (3-fold λ search plus up to 1000 SVDs on the stacked matrix): under 1 h. MIWAE (500 epochs, K=20, latent 10 / hidden 128, CPU): seconds on the small tables, about 3 min on letter and about 7 min on electricity, about 4-6 CPU-h in total. Sinkhorn (500 iterations of a 512×512 tensorized Sinkhorn on CPU): about 1-4 min per run, 10-40 CPU-h for 630 runs, or about 1-3 h if patched to GPU. HyperImpute AutoML (per-column search on 5000 or fewer rows each iteration, up to 40 iterations with patience 5): ReMasker's Table 8 reports 40-298 s per run on 7 datasets (hardware not stated; wiki remasker-paper.md:181). My estimate is 1-15 min per run, spambase and letter at the top, about 10-60 CPU-h serial for 630 runs, about half for the induced population only. It parallelises by dataset, as the backfills already do with dry runs per `--dataset`. These are estimates, not measured on the fork.
cards.gap_exposed: The fork's bar (mean_mode, knn5/knn10, hgb, lgbm) and its external missForest contain no deep generative (GAIN, MIWAE), optimal-transport (Sinkhorn), low-rank (SoftImpute), AutoML iterative (HyperImpute) or MICE imputer. Those are the standard comparison set in ReMasker, CACTI, TabNAT, PMAE and MTabGen, almost always run through this library. HyperImpute is ReMasker's "only close competitor" (wiki remasker-paper.md:156). Since E21 found the tuned model "beats the bar nowhere on induced cells" (docs/EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md:50), HyperImpute is the only addition likely to raise the bar. GAIN and MIWAE are known-weak, so adding them mostly lets TRIDENT beat more rows, which a reviewer could read as padding. A side benefit: the library's `simulate_nan` (MAR logistic; MNAR logistic, quantile and self-masked) could give the fork its first non-MCAR gaps. That is a separate change, and the MNAR variant would have to be fixed explicitly. MICE alone needs no new dependency: scikit-learn's IterativeImputer is already installed.
cards.rq_or_todo: RQ1, whether TRIDENT imputes competitively against dedicated imputers under MCAR/MAR/MNAR (projects/trident/thesis-goals.md:75). It complements BACKLOG I3, ReMasker as a baseline, deferred when ADR 0016 chose missForest (docs/BACKLOG.md:370). Partly todo t1, whose MICE baseline is better taken from scikit-learn (_meta/todos.md:19). Not t3 or step zero, which are classification.
cards.reasons: Yes, one `--no-deps` install puts all five methods in the fork's env, but not as correct same-cell baselines "in a few hours". Five things stand in the way. (1) Protocol mismatch: hyperimpute, Sinkhorn, EM and the GAIN/SoftImpute plugins are transductive, so they need stack-and-slice and a full refit for each population. (2) Three silent plugin bugs change the method: GAIN and SoftImpute ignore their hyperparameters, and MIWAE defaults to a 1-unit network and crashes on a zero scale. (3) The AutoML plugin crashes on the fork's scikit-learn 1.9 through logistic_regression's multi_class unless that learner is dropped from its seeds. (4) Every plugin reseeds the global numpy/torch/random streams, against the fork's stream rule. (5) HyperImpute costs roughly 10-60 CPU-h for the 630 scorings. Add a dormant upstream (last release February 2023) and a TensorFlow dependency pulled in by MIRACLE. A trimmed path is close to QUICK: GAIN, SoftImpute, MIWAE and Sinkhorn on the small variants, induced population only, about 5 h of code plus a few CPU-h. HyperImpute itself is the slow, high-value part.

cards.availability: pip `tabpfn` 9.2.0 (uploaded 2026-10-12; Apache-2.0 code; requires torch>=2.5, huggingface-hub, skrub>=0.7,<0.11, lightgbm>=4.4, pydantic-settings, matplotlib), https://pypi.org/project/tabpfn/ . The API moved fast: 8.0.0 in May 2026, 9.0.0 on 2026-09-15, 9.2.0 on 2026-10-12. Repo active: https://github.com/PriorLabs/TabPFN . WEIGHTS: the package now defaults to TabPFN-3.5, whose weights (like 2.5/2.6/3) carry a NON-COMMERCIAL licence. Downloading them needs a Prior Labs account, licence acceptance and `TABPFN_TOKEN` + `TABPFN_NO_BROWSER=1` on a headless server (https://docs.priorlabs.ai/how-to-access-gated-models.md). The v2 weights are NOT gated: model_loading.py gates only the versions in `_HF_REPOS` (2.5/2.6/3/3.5/3.5-fast). V2 downloads from the public HF repos Prior-Labs/TabPFN-v2-clf and -reg, with a GCS fallback (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PriorLabs/TabPFN/main/src/tabpfn/model_loading.py). v2's licence is 'Prior Labs License' = Apache 2.0 plus an attribution requirement (https://huggingface.co/Prior-Labs/TabPFN-v2-clf). So no account or token is needed if the wrapper calls `TabPFNClassifier.create_default_for_version(ModelVersion.V2)` and pins the package version.
cards.api_fit: Not a BaselineImputer. The fork already has a classification task with no runs: DEFAULT_TASK = "classification" (src/training/types.py:83), the ranking metric f1_macro (types.py:138, src/training/finetuning.py:30), and a classification regression fixture on vehicle_00nan (AGENTS.md:12). The wrapper is a standalone runner on the fork's own folds: prepare_dataset + build_folds (src/training/data.py:47, :182; StratifiedKFold(5, seed), with validation = 0.1/(1-1/5) of train+val, so train ≈ 0.70N, val 0.10N, test 0.20N, data.py:221-227). It fits TabPFNClassifier on train (or train+val: TabPFN has nothing to tune, which is the owner's call) and scores test macro-F1 with finetuning.py's metric function, giving the same 15 fold pairs TRIDENT would use. Encoding: numericals are already StandardScaled (data.py:70-73), which is harmless. Categoricals: pass vocabulary codes plus `categorical_features_indices` (no one-hot, per the README). Map every `_NOT_A_CLASS` value ('nan', '[MASK]', '[NULL]', src/training/imputation_baselines.py:33-34) back to np.nan so TabPFN's native missing handling sees a gap, not a category. Labels have no gaps in the nan variants (checked credit-g_80nan, spambase_60nan, electricity_20nan, letter_20nan: 0 label NaN), so a fair TabPFN-vs-TRIDENT paired comparison needs only a TRIDENT classification run on the same folds. That run does not exist yet and is the expensive half.
cards.categorical_support: Native: categorical features are declared by index, and missing values in them are handled. The 9 tables: credit-g has 13 categorical features (max cardinality 10) and kr-vs-kp is all categorical (max 3). electricity's day column is declared categorical by the fork. A missing value enters as a missing-indicator + fill inside TabPFN (tracker row 18 comment; concepts/imputation-free-learning.md:87, marked unverified there).
cards.feasible_tables: v2 limits: 10,000 training rows, 500 features, and 10 classes (https://docs.priorlabs.ai/models.md); the class cap cannot be overridden. Train ≈ 0.70N, so the variants that fit cleanly are credit-g ×4 (700), kr-vs-kp ×4 (2,237), spambase ×4 (3,221), vehicle ×2 (592), biodeg ×2 (739), kc2 ×2 (365) and pendigits (7,694 rows, or 8,794 with val; exactly 10 classes). That is 19 of 21 variants. letter fails on both rows (14,000) and classes (26): it needs tabpfn-extensions' many-class wrapper plus `ignore_pretraining_limits=True` (out of envelope), or subsampling, or dropping it. electricity fails on rows (31,718): `ignore_pretraining_limits` or a 10k subsample. TabArena applies the same ≤10k/500/10 restriction to TabPFNv2 (https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16791). GPU: gorgona8's RTX 3090 Ti (24 GB) is fine (docs/EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md:668). The Windows RTX 3050 is marginal: the README asks for ~8 GB, and CPU inference is capped at 1,000 samples for pre-v3 models unless TABPFN_ALLOW_CPU_LARGE_DATASET is set.
cards.known_failures: Fork: ADR 0016 rejected 'TabPFN v2.5 per column' because the weights need licence acceptance and an API token, and the ~10k context would subsample letter and electricity (docs/adr/0016-missforest-baselines.md:206-208). The token half is stale for v2: only 2.5+ is gated. The 10k half stands for v2 (v2.5/2.6 actually allow 100k rows, but they are gated and non-commercial). Docs: predict re-runs the whole training context, so batch test rows. The default model is 3.5, so a missing version pin silently triggers a browser login on gorgona8. Wiki: MaskTab set TabPFN-2.5 aside for 'scalability challenges' above 50k samples (references/masktab-paper.md:254). Bertie-Quille: raw NaN into TabPFN v2 about matches imputation pipelines (reading-tracker.csv:175). Global-RNG hygiene is unverified (the fork forbids touching the global streams, imputation_baselines.py:40-42), so save and restore the RNG state around the calls.
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: No numbers pulled. TabArena-v0.1 includes credit-g (OpenML 46918) and qsar-biodeg (46952) and reports TabPFNv2 and TabICL per dataset in Appendix F. Its metric is ROC AUC (binary) on complete data with its own CV, so it is not macro-F1 and only a loose sanity check. Real-TabPFN's TabPFNv2 suite reportedly includes credit-g and kr-vs-kp (search snippet, unverified). TabZilla's raw results (github.com/naszilla/tabzilla) hold TabPFN v1, not v2. None of these match TRIDENT Table 3's setup (seed-42 split).
cards.wrapper_effort: About 6-10 h. Runner over prepare_dataset/build_folds and the '[NULL]'/'nan' to NaN mapping: ~2 h. V2 pin plus a version and checkpoint tag on the MLflow run: ~1 h. letter (many-class wrapper or skip) and electricity (subsample or override) handling: ~2 h. Tests modelled on the vehicle_00nan fixture: ~2 h. MLflow logging under a new tag: ~1 h. The writes must run on gorgona8, the store writer. An ADR note correcting ADR 0016's v2 blocker.
cards.compute_estimate: 21 variants × 15 fold pairs = 315 fit+predict calls. On the 3090 Ti the 19 in-envelope variants take seconds each (≤8.8k context, ≤57 features), so well under 1 GPU-hour. electricity with an override (~32k context, ~9k test rows) and letter through many-class ECOC (several fits per fold) add perhaps 0.5-1 h. Total ≈ 1-2 GPU-hours on gorgona8, shared with training runs (EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md:746). No HPO, by design.
cards.gap_exposed: The fork has no classification number at all, so TRIDENT has never been placed against a tuning-free foundation model on its own variants. The fork's record also overstates the v2 blocker (ADR 0016:206). TabPFN v2's native NaN handling is 'fill + indicator inside a PFN', a ready RQ2 arm against TRIDENT's learned per-column [NULL].
cards.rq_or_todo: Step zero (projects/trident/thesis-goals.md:152) and t3 (rerun Table 3 with ≥5 seeds and equal HPO, _meta/todos.md:21). TabPFN needs no HPO, so it is the cleanest equal-budget baseline. The thesis baseline list names TabPFN v2 and TabICLv2 (thesis-goals.md:146). RQ2 arm: fill + indicator vs [NULL].
cards.reasons: v2 weights are ungated, permissively licensed (Apache + attribution) and auto-downloaded, and the fork's classification path and folds already exist. Cost is ~1-2 GPU-hours and the wrapper is under a day. Caveats: letter (26 classes, 14k rows) and electricity (32k rows) are outside v2's envelope, so report them separately or use TabICLv2 there. The paired verdict needs TRIDENT classification runs on the same folds, and those are the real cost. Pin `tabpfn` and `ModelVersion.V2` explicitly, or the 3.5 default drags in the gated non-commercial weights.

The repo describes the extensions as experimental, 'less rigorously tested than the core tabpfn library' (https://github.com/PriorLabs/tabpfn-extensions). cards.api_fit: Signature: `TabPFNUnsupervisedModel(tabpfn_clf, tabpfn_reg)`, `.fit(X_train)`, `.impute(X, t=1e-9, n_permutations=10)`. impute fills only X's NaN cells, using fit()'s data as context, so it maps onto BaselineImputer (src/training/imputation_baselines.py:54-69): fit on the training fold, impute the test frame. The wrapper must build a float matrix with NaN where `hidden | frame.isna()`, because hidden cells arrive as a boolean mask, not NaN (module docstring :11-13). Categoricals become training-vocabulary codes, with 'nan'/'[MASK]'/'[NULL]' mapped to NaN; GradientBoostingImputer._matrix (:277-293) is the exact template. Pass categorical indices through set_categorical_features. Decode the codes back to as_category_strings strings and return columns in frame order (as at :309-314; score_baselines checks the order at :365). Register a new _Family in baseline_cache.py (:64-73) with libraries ('tabpfn','tabpfn-extensions','torch') and the checkpoint name in the key, since library versions are keyed (:82) but the weights are not. The merge must also be patched to deterministic: numerical cells are sampled from the averaged bar distribution at temperature t, and categorical cells are DRAWN from averaged probabilities (t unused). The output is a sample, not a mean or argmax, which conflicts with the fork's fixed-fill baselines.
cards.categorical_support: Yes: a categorical column uses the classifier when its cardinality is within the classifier's class limit (10 for v2), otherwise the regressor. All the fork's categorical columns are ≤10 (credit-g max 10, kr-vs-kp max 3, electricity day 7). If tabpfn_clf is None and a categorical column needs it, impute raises ValueError.
cards.feasible_tables: The algorithm is feasible on every table except letter and electricity, where the 10k-row v2 context forces subsampling (training folds of 14,000 and 31,718 rows). Compute rules out all 21 variants, though: see compute_estimate. There is no row cap or subsampling in the code, and no explicit device placement (`.numpy()` calls assume CPU tensors). GPU use is unverified, and on CPU pre-v3 models are capped at 1,000 rows.
cards.known_failures: Method code: fits per impute call are bounded by (columns with NaN) × n_permutations × n_features, because each permutation walks every position and refits TabPFN at each position that still has gaps; under per-column MCAR every column has gaps, so the bound is close to tight. Output is stochastic, and the docstring's 'independent' claim contradicts the sequential conditioning. Wiki: column-wise TabPFN imputation is about 100× slower per entry than TabImpute (references/tabimpute-paper.md:127), and TabImpute's MissBench tables were only 50-235 rows (tabimpute-paper.md:111). The tracker notes that TabPFN v2 'does not output imputations (separate tabpfn-extensions imputer)' (reading-tracker.csv:18).
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: none found for the 9 tables. Column-wise TabPFN appears in TabImpute's MissBench (41-42 small numeric OpenML tables ≤235 rows), where it is the best method on Pol-MNAR (RMSE 2.295 vs TabImpute 2.680; references/tabimpute-paper.md:120, :125). Neither the tables nor the metric match (RMSE, not impute_score).
cards.wrapper_effort: About 8-12 h: BaselineImputer adapter on the hgb matrix template (~3 h), deterministic-merge patch or subclass of impute_ (~3 h), device and limit handling plus letter/electricity subsampling (~2 h), cache family and backfill script modelled on scripts/backfill_lgbm_baseline.py (~2 h), tests (~2 h). The code is not the blocker.
cards.compute_estimate: Fit upper bound per impute call, cols × 10 × cols: credit-g 4,000; kr-vs-kp 12,960; spambase 32,490; vehicle 3,240; biodeg 16,810; kc2 4,410; pendigits 2,560; letter 2,560; electricity 640. Summed over the 21 variants that is ≈252k TabPFN fit+predicts per fold and population. × 15 fold pairs × 2 populations (induced, masked) ≈ 7.6M calls. At ~0.5 s each on the 3090 Ti that is about 1,000 GPU-hours (~6 weeks). fast_mode (1 permutation) gives ≈760k calls, ~100 GPU-hours, and still returns one sample from one ordering.
cards.gap_exposed: Would place TRIDENT's decoder against a foundation-model imputer (the RQ1 comparator class). The extension is the wrong vehicle: its cost is quadratic in columns, and its sampled output breaks the fork's deterministic, cached-baseline protocol.
cards.rq_or_todo: RQ1 (TRIDENT as an imputer vs dedicated imputers incl. TabImpute, projects/trident/thesis-goals.md:75); ADR 0016's deferred list.
cards.reasons: At ~1,000 GPU-hours with default settings, or ~100 in fast mode, the extension is infeasible across 21 variants × 15 folds × 2 populations. Its output is a stochastic sample, so the merge needs patching to fit the fork's fixed-fill baselines. It is experimental, its compatibility with tabpfn 9.x is unverified, it pulls in telemetry, and it has no device handling. v2's 10k context still subsamples letter and electricity. The practical TabPFN imputation route is the column-wise subclass on the next card.
evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PriorLabs/tabpfn-extensions/main/src/tabpfn_extensions/unsupervised/unsupervised.py (impute(X, t=1e-9, n_permutations=10); loop cols × permutations × positions; sampled merge; no device placement)

cards.name: Column-wise TabPFN v2 imputer in the hgb recipe (subclass, no extension)
cards.availability: Same `tabpfn` 9.2.0 package with v2 weights, ungated (see the classifier card). No tabpfn-extensions and no telemetry dependency. The extensions' many-class wrapper is not needed: every categorical target column has ≤10 classes.
cards.api_fit: Exactly the LightGbmImputer pattern (src/training/lightgbm_baseline.py:30-61): subclass GradientBoostingImputer and override only `_fit_one` to return TabPFNRegressor / TabPFNClassifier (create_default_for_version(ModelVersion.V2), random_state=BOOSTING_SEED, categorical_features_indices from `categorical`). fit, _matrix and impute are inherited: NaN where hidden or missing, categoricals as vocabulary codes, decoded to strings, frame column order. That yields one model per column, a single pass, deterministic fills, and the same cells as the bar. Two decisions for the owner: (1) the hgb recipe doubles every column's training rows with a 20%-hidden copy (imputation_baselines.py:47-51, :241-244). TabPFN's prior already contains NaN, so the copy may be unnecessary, and it pushes pendigits past 10k rows (0.8×7,694×2 ≈ 12.3k); override fit to drop it or cap the context. (2) letter (~11.2k observed rows per column without the copy) and electricity (~25k) exceed the context: subsample with a fixed stream or use ignore_pretraining_limits. A new _Family in baseline_cache.py (:64-73) keyed on tabpfn and torch versions plus the checkpoint name; save and restore the global RNG state around TabPFN calls, since its RNG hygiene is unverified.
cards.categorical_support: Categorical features are declared by index, and categorical targets are predicted by TabPFNClassifier on vocabulary codes. All fork categorical columns have ≤10 categories (credit-g max 10, kr-vs-kp 3, electricity day 7), within v2's class cap.
cards.feasible_tables: 19 of 21 variants run inside v2's envelope if the 20% copy is dropped (pendigits: ~6.2k observed rows per column). letter (11.2k) is slightly over and electricity (25k) well over: subsample or override, and flag them. These are the very tables where ADR 0016 says the bar decides (docs/adr/0016-missforest-baselines.md:206-208). Needs the 3090 Ti on gorgona8.
cards.known_failures: As on the extension card, minus the cost: TabImpute reports column-wise TabPFN at about 100× its own per-entry cost (references/tabimpute-paper.md:127), but on this protocol there is one fit per column per fold, not a permutation sweep. Column-wise TabPFN predicts the mean or argmax per cell, so it is comparable to hgb/lgbm. Each predict re-runs the context.
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: none found for the 9 tables. MissBench column-wise TabPFN numbers are in references/tabimpute-paper.md:120 (small tables, RMSE).
cards.wrapper_effort: About 5-8 h: _fit_one override (~1 h, the LightGBM subclass is 72 lines), fit override for the copy and context cap (~1-2 h), cache family plus a backfill script cloned from scripts/backfill_lgbm_baseline.py (~2 h), tests (~1-2 h), an ADR amending ADR 0016's TabPFN entry.
cards.compute_estimate: Column models per fold set, summed over the 21 variants: 4×(20+36+57) + 2×(18+41+21) + 16+16+8 = 652. That gives 652 × 15 ≈ 9.8k fits, with one predict per population, so ≈19.6k predicts. At ~1 s for the small tables, plus ~5 s for letter and ~15 s for electricity columns, the total is ≈6-10 GPU-hours on the 3090 Ti, uncertain by about 2×. That is in the range of the deferred ReMasker backfill (~40 GPU-hours, ADR 0016:195-198), not of the extension.
cards.gap_exposed: The baseline bar is all trees/kNN, so it lacks a foundation-model imputer scored on exactly the decoder's cells, the comparator class RQ1 names (TabImpute is TabPFN-like).
cards.rq_or_todo: RQ1 (projects/trident/thesis-goals.md:75); reopens ADR 0016's rejected 'TabPFN per column' entry, whose token blocker no longer applies to v2.
cards.reasons: The fit to the BaselineImputer protocol is clean (the LightGBM subclass is the template) and v2 is ungated. Cost is ~6-10 GPU-hours. It is MEDIUM rather than QUICK because of the context-size decisions on pendigits, letter and electricity, a new cache family plus backfill on gorgona8, and the protocol call on the 20% hidden copy, which needs an ADR.

cards.name: TabICLv2 classifier (soda-inria tabicl)
cards.availability: pip `tabicl` 2.2.0 (2026-09-02), BSD-3-Clause (Soda team @ Inria; the forecast submodule is Apache-2.0), https://pypi.org/project/tabicl/ . Light dependencies: einops, huggingface-hub, numpy, psutil, scikit-learn>=1.3, scipy, torch>=2.2, tqdm. Weights auto-download from the HF repo jingang/TabICL (bsd-3-clause, no gate seen): https://huggingface.co/jingang/TabICL . Default checkpoints are tabicl-classifier-v2-20260212.ckpt and tabicl-regressor-v2-20260212.ckpt. No account, no token, no telemetry mentioned. Paper: ICML 2026, arXiv 2602.11139 (tracker row 19).
cards.api_fit: Same standalone classification runner as the TabPFN card, on the fork's folds (data.py:182) with test macro-F1 (finetuning.py:30). `TabICLClassifier(n_estimators=8, device=None→CUDA, use_amp='auto', kv_cache=False).fit/predict`, sklearn style. Pass a pandas frame: string/object/category columns are auto-detected and ordinal-encoded. Map '[NULL]'/'[MASK]'/'nan' to real NaN, or TabICL will treat the marker as a category; for a missing categorical that is nearly harmless, since TabICL gives missing its own category anyway. A numerical gap must be NaN. `support_many_classes=True` covers letter. TabICLRegressor exists, so a column-wise imputer in the hgb recipe is possible too, but TabICL mean-fills feature gaps with no indicator.
cards.categorical_support: Native for pandas input: categorical columns are ordinal-encoded and missing is its own category. Numerical NaN is mean-imputed internally, with no indicator.
cards.feasible_tables: All 9 tables and 21 variants without subsampling: pre-trained on 300 to 48K training samples and 2 to 100 columns, benchmarked up to 100K rows; the fork's largest training fold is electricity at 31,718 and the widest table spambase at 57 features. letter's 26 classes go through support_many_classes. kc2 (365 train rows) is near the untested <300 regime. GPU: the 3090 Ti is fine; complexity is O(n² + nm²).
cards.known_failures: Docs: accuracy may degrade 'when going much beyond 100 features' (not an issue here), and datasets under 300 samples are untested. Wiki: TabICLv2 mean-fills missing values, and its authors say missing indicators and missingness-aware pre-training remain unexplored (reading-tracker.csv:19). Under informative missingness it sees no missingness signal on numerical columns, which is the point for RQ2. Jeon 2026 (JEPA recipe on the TabICL prior) found a latent JEPA term trailing value-only training (reading-tracker.csv:140).
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: No numbers pulled. TabArena-v0.1, where TabICLv2 is reported, includes credit-g and qsar-biodeg (ROC AUC, complete data). TabICLv2 places second by average rank (4.43) on TabArena's 24 binary datasets (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.11139, per the search snippet). Per-dataset values were not retrieved.
cards.wrapper_effort: About 4-6 h if built after the TabPFN runner (shared harness; only the estimator and NaN mapping differ), about 6-8 h standalone.
cards.compute_estimate: 21 × 15 = 315 fit+predict calls. The README gives under 10 s for 50k×100 on an H100; on a 3090 Ti, assume roughly 3-5× slower for electricity and seconds for the rest. Total under 1 GPU-hour on gorgona8.
cards.gap_exposed: Same as TabPFN: no classification number in the fork. It also gives a 'mean-fill, no indicator' foundation model to set against TRIDENT's [NULL] on the 60-80% variants.
cards.rq_or_todo: Step zero and t3 (thesis-goals.md:152, _meta/todos.md:21); thesis baseline list (thesis-goals.md:146); RQ2 arm (mean-fill without indicator vs [NULL]); t1 framing at 60-80nan (_meta/todos.md:19).
cards.reasons: Permissive, ungated and lightweight, and it covers all 21 variants with no subsampling, including letter (26 classes) and electricity (32k rows), where TabPFN v2 falls outside its envelope. Under 1 GPU-hour and under a day of code. Its NaN handling (mean-fill, missing-as-category) is itself a useful contrast for RQ2. Like TabPFN, it is only half a comparison until TRIDENT classification runs exist on the same folds.
evidence: https://github.com/soda-inria/tabicl (v2 checkpoints, NaN handling, 48K pre-training range, support_many_classes, H100 timing)

cards.name: TabImpute (Feitelberg et al., arXiv 2510.02625 v6): zero-shot pre-trained Transformer imputer, MCAR default checkpoint; plus the MissBench MNAR specialists and generators
cards.availability: Code: https://github.com/jacobf18/tabular (public, licence null, 9 stars, 4 open issues, last push 2026-10-15). The repo changes almost daily with experimental model families (MatrixFormer, RaBEL, DWIP) that are not in the paper. PyPI: `tabimpute` 0.0.4 (2026-03-07), no licence field, Python >=3.9,<3.13. It hard-pins `tabpfn==6.0.0` (mcpfn/pyproject.toml:34), and tabpfn 6.0.0 needs `scikit-learn<1.8` plus tabpfn-common-utils[telemetry-interactive], under the Prior Labs licence (Apache-derived; internal benchmarking is exempt from its attribution clause). The fork's locked env has scikit-learn 1.9.0, torch 2.5.1+cu121 and Python 3.11, so sklearn is a hard conflict and the rest fits. Weights: HF Tabimpute/TabImpute, Apache-2.0, not gated. `tabimpute_001.ckpt` (133 MB) is the paper's default model: `ImputePFN()` loads it, and MissBench's 'tabimpute' method uses that default. The repo also holds `tabimputev2.ckpt` (807 MB) and the MatrixFormer experts (312 MB each, a later direct model with 2000x1000 windows; not the paper's model). No pattern-specialist (MNAR) checkpoint is published: the benchmark README says 'These checkpoints are not on HuggingFace. Train them with the scripts in mcpfn/scripts'. Pin a git commit, not PyPI: the HF card names 2cf54ac and warns an older PyPI release may lack APIs. No Prior Labs token is needed, because TabImpute loads its own checkpoint, not TabPFN weights. That token was what blocked TabPFN in ADR 0016.
cards.api_fit: It fits the BaselineImputer protocol (imputation_baselines.py:54-69) as an external family, like missForest, logged beside the bar but not part of it (missforest.py:1-9). `fit` is close to a no-op. TabImpute learns nothing per table and imputes in context from the observed cells of the matrix it is given (ImputePFN.impute, interface.py:1012-1037). So fit(train_frame) only stores the training fold's category vocabulary (excluding _NOT_A_CLASS = {'nan','[MASK]','[NULL]'}, imputation_baselines.py:33-34) and the training means and stds, which are passed as impute(X, means=, stds=). impute(frame, hidden): build the matrix exactly like KnnImputer._matrix (imputation_baselines.py:148-160). Numeric columns stay as they are (already scaled), each categorical column becomes a one-hot block over the training vocabulary, and NaN goes where `hidden | frame.isna()`, the whole block for a categorical cell. Call ImputePFN with row chunking (max_num_rows; overlapping tail windows averaged, interface.py:1133-1160, re-normalized per chunk at :1348). Decode each block by argmax, as KnnImputer does (:170-177), and return floats and strings in frame order. Register a `_Family('tabimpute', (imputation_baselines, imputation_metrics, tabimpute_baseline), (...), fit_tabimpute_imputers)` in baseline_cache.py:64-73, and backfill with BaselineScorer(families=('tabimpute',)) (baseline_cache.py:96), adapting scripts/backfill_lgbm_baseline.py. Four protocol decisions: (1) Env. It can't be installed into the fork's venv without downgrading sklearn. That would move every cache key (baseline_cache.py:77-82 hashes version('scikit-learn')) and the hgb/knn fills already in the store. So it needs a separate venv and a subprocess/.npy bridge, and the family's cache key has to carry the pinned commit and checkpoint sha rather than an importable version. (2) Transductive. ADR 0016 rejected HyperImpute for being transductive on the test fold (docs/adr/0016-missforest-baselines.md:202-204). Here the choice is the test fold as context with training stats passed, or [train; test] stacked, which multiplies the cells by about 5 and breaks feasibility beyond the small tables. (3) RNG. The paper's setting wraps the model in 4 random permutation preprocessors (MissBench methods.py:77) that call global np.random.permutation (prepreocess.py:53, 69, 86-87). Use preprocessors=None (one deterministic pass, not the paper's setting) or save and restore np.random state; the fork never touches the global streams (imputation_baselines.py:40-43). (4) Point estimate. The default is the median; the fork's numeric score is RMSE (imputation_metrics.py:49-52, 82), for which prediction_stat='mean' is the right choice. bf16 inference drifts in the last digits across GPUs, which the cache tolerates because it keys on hostname.
cards.categorical_support: None validated. The model is pre-trained on continuous low-rank synthetic tables, and the paper lists categorical data as future work (paper v6 snapshot lines 1040-1046). The HF card says inputs must be numeric and categoricals encoded separately. The repo's TabImputeCategorical (interface.py:2029ff) one-hot encodes, imputes and takes the argmax, but it builds the vocabulary from the frame it fills (interface.py:2087), which breaks the fork's rule that the training fold fixes the vocabulary. The authors' benchmark/categorical/README.md calls those scripts unmaintained and broken against the current package. Workaround: the one-hot block with argmax decode, mirroring KnnImputer. Out of distribution for credit-g (13 of 20 columns categorical, about 61 one-hot columns), kr-vs-kp (all 36 columns categorical and binary or ternary, about 73 one-hot columns) and electricity (day, 7 levels, about 14 columns). Any categorical score there is an engineering result, not the method as published.
cards.feasible_tables: Sized on the test fold the fork scores (decoding.py:179, about 1/5 of rows), with test_rows x one-hot columns compared to the paper's maximum of 235x33, about 7.7k cells, numeric only (MissBench datasets.py:5-9, 50-250 rows). In regime, single pass, numeric: kc2 (~104x21, 2.2k cells; 2 variants), vehicle (~169x18, 3.0k; 2), biodeg (~211x41, 8.7k; 2), so 6 of 21 variants. Near the size limit but mixed-type: credit-g (~200x61 one-hot, 12k; 4 variants). Out of regime, needing row chunks of about 200-250 rows, so each window sees only part of the fold: kr-vs-kp (~639x73, 47k, all categorical; 4), spambase (~920x57, 52k; 4), pendigits (~2198x16, 35k; 1), letter (~4000x16, 64k; 1), electricity (~9062x14, 127k; 1). My estimate (not measured): EWF turns an m x n chunk into mn items with (m+n+2)/2 feature tokens over 12 layers of width 192 (mcpfn.py:94-97, config.py:44), all items attending to each other. A whole pendigits fold (~39M tokens) cannot fit in 24 GB; 250-row chunks need roughly 5-10 GB. So with chunking, all 21 variants should run on gorgona8's RTX 3090 Ti (24 GB). The Windows RTX 3050 Laptop (4 GB) is limited to tiny chunks. Stacking train and test as context is infeasible beyond the small tables (letter about 320k cells). None of this is verified; the reference smoke test is mcpfn/scripts/benchmark_tabimpute_runtime_scaling.py (legacy model, 10 columns, 10-1000 rows). The 2000x1000 windows in evaluate_chunked_uci.py are for the direct MatrixFormer model, not this checkpoint. MNAR specialists are not feasible on any table without first training them.
cards.known_failures: From the wiki (references/tabimpute-paper.md): the evaluation stops at 235 rows and 33 numeric columns, and the mn expansion caps size. There are no seeds and no repeated masks; the CIs span datasets only and are sometimes wider than the gaps they compare (Pol-MNAR 2.680 ± 1.318). Baseline settings are unstated, and ReMasker and CACTI ran outside their regime. It loses Pol-MNAR to column-wise TabPFN (2.680 vs 2.295) and ties K-NN on Col-MAR and Phase-MNAR. Specialists collapse off-pattern: on MCAR the Self-MNAR specialist scores 1.135, Soft-Pol 1.653 and Censor 2.259, against 0.819 for the default. The NN, Latent, Block and Clust specialists don't beat the default even on their own patterns. Mixing mechanisms in one pre-training run failed (forgetting, or the model focusing only on Self-MNAR). The paper has no natural missingness, no downstream task and no outcome-dependent MNAR. From the method's docs: the categorical code is unmaintained and broken (benchmark/categorical/README.md). The HF card warns that entirely missing rows or columns have limited support and that patterns outside the synthetic prior reduce accuracy. CPU is slow, 'a few minutes per table' at ≤235 rows (benchmark README). Row and column indices are input features, so results depend on order; that is why the paper uses the permutation ensemble. The default reads the global numpy RNG and bf16 drifts across GPUs. PyPI and main diverge, and main changes almost daily.
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: None per table. MissBench's 41-42 OpenML tables are all-numeric, 50-250 rows, and none of the fork's 9 is among them (datasets.py:5-9). The repo's secondary UCI suite (HyperImpute protocol, MCAR 0.1-0.5, 10 masks) includes letter_recognition (UCI 59) and spam_base (UCI 94) (datasets.py:90, 95), but I found no per-dataset TabImpute number in the paper or the repo docs. MATRIXFORMER_PLUS_RESULTS.md gives only aggregate UCI NRMSE for later MatrixFormer models (UCI overall 1.016 / 1.157 / 0.998). The metric also differs: per-column RMSE divided by the std of the true missing values, against the fork's RMSE ratio to mean/mode on the same cells. A rough directional check only (my inference): on MissBench MCAR the default scores 0.819 normalized RMSE, where a mean fill sits near 1.0 on that metric. So expect a numeric impute_score below 1 on the in-regime tables, with no claim about whether it clears hgb/lgbm/knn.
cards.wrapper_effort: About 12-20 hours. Module tabimpute_baseline.py, ~120-180 lines: fit stores the vocabulary and stats; impute builds the one-hot matrix with NaNs, calls the model with chunking and decodes, a near copy of KnnImputer._matrix and its decode; ~4-6 h. Separate venv (pinned commit plus checkpoint sha, offline HF download to gorgona8, TABPFN telemetry turned off) and a subprocess/.npy bridge or persistent worker, since the sklearn<1.8 pin rules out the fork's venv; ~4 h. _Family registration with a cache key that has no importable version, and a backfill limited to families=('tabimpute',) adapted from scripts/backfill_lgbm_baseline.py (387 lines); ~3-4 h. Unit tests on a toy mixed frame (order of columns, categorical decode, hidden-plus-NaN union, unchanged global RNG state) and a one-fold GPU timing and memory smoke test on gorgona8 for each large table; ~3-5 h. Excluded: MNAR specialists (pre-training each one is 10-15 h on an H200 per paper v6 lines 511-512, likely days on a 3090 Ti), and porting the MissBench generators (about 1 day, see rq_or_todo).
cards.compute_estimate: Zero-shot, so there is no per-fold fit. Each (fold, population) pair is computed once and cached for every arm. Populations per fold: masked (decoding.py:212), induced (:256), plus the multi-rate at_rate loop when it is enabled (:241). That is at least 21 variants x 15 fold pairs x 2 = 630 impute calls, more with multi-rate. My FLOP-based estimate for gorgona8's RTX 3090 Ti (not measured): small tables 1-5 s per call; credit-g ~4 s; kr-vs-kp and spambase ~20 s (3-4 chunks); pendigits ~10 s, letter ~20 s, electricity ~40 s (9, 16 and 37 chunks of 250 rows). Total roughly 2-8 GPU-hours for one deterministic pass, and about 4x that with the paper's 4-permutation ensemble. Plus a one-time 133 MB download. A GPU is required. Run it as an offline backfill, not inside live training on gorgona8, which shares VRAM. Check with one timing run on spambase and electricity before committing to any of this.
cards.gap_exposed: The fork's bar (mean_mode, knn5/10, hgb, lgbm, plus external missForest) is made only of methods fit on the training fold: trees and neighbours. There is no pre-trained Transformer imputer, which is the family a reviewer will compare TRIDENT's decoder with first. TabImpute is the strongest published zero-shot imputer for small tables. It would show whether TRIDENT's per-table masked training beats in-context imputation from a prior. It would also show the size-regime gap: the fork's test folds are 1-16x MissBench's largest table and its full tables up to 190x, so a result reported by table size tells where pre-training priors stop helping. Secondary: TabImpute encodes a missing input as mean fill plus a binary indicator inside a Transformer, a ready 'mean + indicator' comparator for TRIDENT's learned per-column [NULL] (RQ2). It also exposes that the fork has no MNAR code at all: grep finds 'mnar' only in docs, none in src/.
cards.rq_or_todo: RQ1 (thesis-goals.md:75 names TabImpute among the dedicated imputers to beat), with 'report by table size' (tabimpute-paper.md:150). Owner calls before any code: (a) external family, not part of the bar, per the ADR 0016/0017 precedent; (b) context: test fold only with training stats, versus stacked train and test; the latter is feasible only for kc2, vehicle and biodeg; (c) preprocessors=None versus the paper's 4-permutation ensemble with the global RNG saved and restored; (d) prediction_stat mean (fits RMSE) versus median (the paper's default); (e) whether categorical tables are reported, or flagged as out of distribution. RQ4: MNAR specialists are NOT_QUICK (no published weights, 10-15 H200-hours each). Reuse Table 2's matched and mismatched grid as a template, not the weights. Separate small todo for the MNAR arm: port, rather than import, 6 MissBench generators from mcpfn/src/tabimpute/prior/training_set_generation.py. They are Self-MNAR (:609-626), Pol (:834-846), Soft-Pol (:848-876), Cluster (:1045-1078), Censor (:1105-1129) and Two-Phase (:1158-1191), 10-35 lines each. Importing is ruled out: the module is 2,535 lines importing sklearn GP, scipy, a diffusion module and the full package with its sklearn pin, the code is unlicensed so it should be re-implemented from App. A.3 and cited, and it uses global np/torch seeds (patterns.py:161-175).
