cards.availability: PyPI `macode` 1.0.1 (uploaded 2025-09-04; earlier 0.1.0 to 0.2.4 all on 2024-12-19), MIT, requires-python >=3.10,<4. The wheel pins exact versions: torch==2.2.2, numpy==1.26.4, pandas==2.2.3, scikit-learn==1.6.0, plus wandb, geomloss, seaborn, statsmodels (https://pypi.org/pypi/macode/json). The fork's lock has torch 2.5.1+cu121, numpy 2.4.6, pandas 2.3.3 and scikit-learn 1.9.0 (uv.lock:3276-3277, 1816-1817, 2231-2232, 2896-2897). So `uv add macode` would downgrade the fork, and it would also invalidate every baseline-cache entry, because the cache key hashes the scikit-learn, pandas and numpy versions (src/training/baseline_cache.py:82). The repo github.com/an-seunghwan/MaCoDE is MIT and not archived: 5 stars, 2 forks, 0 open issues, last push 2025-09-04 (commit 8867879, the one the wiki read), 25 commits (https://api.github.com/repos/an-seunghwan/MaCoDE). At runtime the code imports only torch, numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, scipy and tqdm (macode/__init__.py is empty), all already in the fork's venv. Recommendation: vendor macode/model.py and the parts of dataset.py and macode.py you need (about 400 lines, MIT notice kept) under src/training/, rather than pip-installing.
cards.api_fit:
Plugs in as a fourth baseline family that implements BaselineImputer (src/training/imputation_baselines.py:54-69: fit(frame), then impute(frame, hidden) returns every hidden or missing cell filled, in z-space for numbers and as the strings as_category_strings renders for categories, without rewriting the frame). It is fit once per fold, like fit_lightgbm_imputers (src/training/lightgbm_baseline.py:64-72) and fit_missforest_imputers (src/training/missforest.py:262-270). It is registered as a new _Family in baseline_cache.py:64-73 with libraries=("torch",), and added to summary.py:88 EXTERNAL_BASELINES so it gets gap_to_macode and stays out of the bar, the way ADR 0017 treats missForest.

The stock API does not fit as it stands:
(1) `MaCoDE.impute(tau)` only fills `self.dataset`, the frame the model was built on. It takes no new frame, and dataset.py has no transform and stores no category-to-code mapping. Using it transductively (fitting on train plus test with the hidden cells as NaN) would break "fit on the training fold alone" (imputation_baselines.py:5-6, missforest.py:76-87) and would need one fit per population. So the wrapper must be inductive. fit() builds the training-fold vocabulary exactly as hgb does (imputation_baselines.py:219-227, excluding _NOT_A_CLASS), encodes categories as 0..K-1 codes, passes numbers as they are (z-space; the QuantileTransformer does not care about monotone scaling), and calls train(). impute() reuses `dataset.scalers[col]` and `dataset.bins` to give continuous cells bin indices 1..L, gives categories code+1 (an unseen category becomes 0, as hgb treats it as a gap), sets hidden or NaN cells to 0 (the [MASK]/missing word), and runs batched forward passes under no_grad. It then decodes the cells itself and maps codes back to class strings.
(2) Decode policy. The stock impute samples a bin, then draws uniformly inside it. The fork scores RMSE in z-space and categorical accuracy (src/training/imputation_metrics.py:49-56, 82-86), so a single draw adds pure variance and is penalized. Use the posterior mean, Σ_l p_l·m_l, where m_l is the training-fold mean of the observed values in bin l (fall back to the inverse CDF of the bin midpoint for an empty bin), and argmax for categories. Optionally log the stock sampled draw as a second arm, `macode_draw`.
(3) Pass a copy of the frame. CustomDataset writes category codes back into the caller's DataFrame in place. That would break the "frame never rewritten" contract (imputation_baselines.py:67) and the cache key, which hashes train_frame (baseline_cache.py:154).
(4) RNG isolation (the global-stream rule is in imputation_baselines.py:40-43 and missforest.py:54-57; see known_failures). Wrap every MaCoDE call to save and restore the torch, CUDA, numpy and random states and the cudnn flags, for example with torch.random.fork_rng, and use a fixed MACODE_SEED=0 like BOOSTING_SEED.
(5) Use the paper's settings, not the class defaults: bins=50, dim_transformer=128, 4 heads, 2 layers, 500 epochs, batch 1024, AdamW with lr 1e-3 and weight decay 1e-3. The vendored code needs that last change, because the stock optimizer is Adam with no weight decay.
No "nan" marker or extra scaling is needed beyond this; frames come in StandardScaled (src/training/data.py:66-72).
cards.categorical_support: Native. Each categorical column has its own nn.Embedding(K+1, d) with row 0 as [MASK]/missing, and a K-way softmax head. Categories must be integer-coded by the caller; the stock dataset uses pandas cat.codes+1 and returns codes, not labels, so the wrapper owns the vocabulary and the decode. Continuous columns are discretized into L quantile bins of the training fold's empirical CDF, fit on observed values only. Integer-valued or heavily tied columns (letter 0-15, pendigits, kc2 counts) collapse onto a few bins, which is harmless. Unpatched, the code requires both kinds of column to be present (see known_failures).
cards.feasible_tables: All 21 variants once the empty-branch guard is patched (see known_failures). Memory is no constraint: at most 57 tokens per row (spambase), d=128, batch 1024, and default dim_feedforward 2048 come to roughly 1-2 GB of activations, which fits even the 4 GB Windows RTX 3050 and trivially the gorgona8 RTX 3090 Ti (docs/EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md:668). Unpatched, only the two mixed-type tables run: credit-g (4 variants) and electricity (1 variant), 5 of 21. Features exclude the label (src/training/data.py:42-44), so spambase, vehicle, biodeg, kc2, pendigits and letter have no categorical column, and kr-vs-kp has no continuous one (all 36 features declared in datasets/categorical_columns/kr-vs-kp.txt). The 60/80nan variants train fine, because the loss only covers observed cells that were masked, but MaCoDE's behaviour at high missingness is barely documented (see known_failures). Only a column with no observed value in a training fold, impossible in practice at these sizes, would need a guard (the QuantileTransformer cannot fit an empty column), mirroring hgb's constant fallback.
cards.known_failures:
From the wiki (references/macode-paper.md):
- The code defaults differ from the paper: bins=10, d=512, 8 heads, 1 layer, 1000 epochs, Adam with no weight decay (line 100).
- The theory covers MAR only; the MNAR results are empirical (line 115).
- No RMSE or MAE is ever reported (lines 149, 172; Remark 3 at _raw/_archived/MaCoDE_2405-20602v2.md:2398).
- Above 30% the only evidence is the kings sweep, where F1 falls below the complete-data baselines from 50% missingness (line 136).
- Nothing was tuned (line 155).

From the code at 8867879, read through WebFetch paraphrase. The empty-branch crash should be confirmed when vendoring, though two fetches agree with the wiki's reading of model.py.
(a) Embedding.forward runs torch.stack over each feature group, so a table with no continuous or no categorical column raises "stack expects a non-empty TensorList". That hits 7 of the 9 tables.
(b) impute() is transductive only, and there is no transform for new data.
(c) CustomDataset mutates the caller's DataFrame in place.
(d) set_random_seed reseeds the global torch, CUDA, numpy and random streams and sets cudnn.deterministic=True and benchmark=False for the whole process. It is called in __init__ and in train(). This violates the fork's rule that baselines never touch global streams, and would leak into a live training run.
(e) impute() never reseeds, so its draws depend on the leftover RNG state.
(f) impute() samples one draw, which inflates RMSE.
(g) The DataLoader builds each row through a per-row __getitem__ (torch.FloatTensor), which adds Python overhead on the large tables.
(h) GPU training (atomic adds in the embedding backward) is not bit-reproducible, so its cache entries are machine-specific like hgb's (baseline_cache.py:9-10), and a backfill cannot verify it to 1e-9.
(i) Exact dependency pins (see availability).
(j) The tau<=0 check in generate_data lacks a raise; this does not matter for imputation.

Table 11 (snapshot line 4314) reports the utility of synthetic data from a MaCoDE trained at 30% missingness, as SMAPE / F1 on letter: MCAR .107±.000 / .674±.004; MAR .107 / .682; MNARL .108 / .676; MNARQ .107 / .676. So no imputation-accuracy number exists for any of the 9 OpenML tables, and there is no published value to sanity-check impute_score against.
cards.wrapper_effort:
About 10-14 hours, 1.5-2 days:
- Vendor model.py and the dataset and training logic with the MIT notice; guard the empty branches, switch to AdamW (weight decay 1e-3), drop the global reseeding (use torch.Generator and np.random.Generator streams, or fork_rng with the cudnn flags saved and restored), and stop the in-place mutation: 2-3 h.
- MacodeImputer.fit and impute: hgb-style vocabulary, test-frame encoding through the stored scalers and bin edges, hidden or missing cells set to 0, batched no_grad forward, posterior-mean or argmax decode, codes mapped back to strings, device choice: 3-4 h, about 150 lines.
- Cache _Family with torch in libraries, and summary EXTERNAL_BASELINES plus gap_to_macode: about 1 h.
- Unit tests on tiny mixed, all-numeric and all-categorical frames: the frame is untouched, the global RNG state is untouched, only hidden cells change, column order is kept, and CPU fills are deterministic: about 2 h.
- Backfill script for an external baseline, modelled on scripts/backfill_lgbm_baseline.py (387 lines) but simpler because the bar is not re-chosen, dry-run first, applied on gorgona8 because it is the store writer: 2-4 h.
cards.compute_estimate:
Inductive, one fit per (variant, seed, fold): 21 × 15 = 315 fits. Fitting per population would double that. Steps per fit = 500 epochs × ceil(0.8n / 1024) training batches, with 0.8n training rows:
- credit-g, vehicle, biodeg, kc2: 500 steps each
- kr-vs-kp: about 1,500
- spambase: about 2,000
- pendigits: about 4,500
- letter: about 8,000
- electricity: about 18,000
That is about 49.5k steps per (seed, fold) and about 0.74M steps in all.

FLOPs, assuming d=128, 2 layers and PyTorch's default dim_feedforward=2048: about 7 MFLOP per token for forward plus backward, and about 1e9 tokens per (seed, fold), so about 1.1e17 FLOP in total. Spambase × 4 rates and kr-vs-kp × 4 dominate, then electricity and letter. There is extra Python overhead from the per-column embedding, head and loss loops (about 115 small modules per step on spambase) and from per-row DataLoader fetches (about 0.7e9 row fetches in all).
- gorgona8 RTX 3090 Ti (about 15-20 TFLOPS effective in fp32): roughly 3-5 GPU-hours serial, easily split across processes given 24 GB. The largest fits take about 1-2 minutes (electricity, spambase); the small tables take seconds.
- Windows RTX 3050 Laptop, 4 GB (about 2 TFLOPS effective): roughly 15-25 hours.
- CPU only: impractical for the large tables (over 100 hours), fine for credit-g, vehicle, kc2 and biodeg.
The package defaults (d=512, 1000 epochs) would cost about 5× more. The paper's own runs were on an NVIDIA A10 (snapshot line 938).
cards.gap_exposed: The fork's bar is entirely non-neural (mean_mode, knn5, knn10, hgb, lgbm), and its only external comparison is missForest. No published deep or Transformer imputer is scored on the decoder's cells. MaCoDE is TRIDENT's nearest prior art: a masked Transformer over cells with a learned per-column [MASK] vector that is also used for missing cells (merged, with no [NULL]/[MASK] split), a value-space target (cross-entropy over quantile bins) rather than TRIDENT's latent JEPA target, and a single training stage (macode-paper.md:88-92, 163). Scoring it under the same 15 paired fold pairs would show whether TRIDENT's split token, latent pre-training and tuned decoder beat a merged-token density model of comparable size. That is the positioning claim the wiki says is unablated (hot.md:23). It would also settle the open question of whether the bin target is accurate as well as well-calibrated (macode-paper.md:172). Caveat for the write-up: the protocol scores MaCoDE on a metric its authors chose not to optimize (Remark 3), so report the posterior-mean decode as the fair arm and the sampled draw separately. Its hyperparameters are untuned, as the fork's baselines are by design (imputation_baselines.py:36-38), while TRIDENT is Optuna-tuned. Say so.

cards.name: ReMasker (Du, Melis & Wang, ICLR 2024)
cards.availability: No PyPI package (searched 2026-10-16). Code: github.com/alps-lab/remasker, 4 commits, 6 stars, 2 open issues, no LICENSE file and no setup.py or pyproject; the wiki read it at commit b2eca0e (2024-05-21). Dependencies are unpinned: torch (cu116 index), timm, hyperimpute. It is not one of HyperImpute's plugins: hyperimpute 0.1.17 (last release 2023-02-28, MIT) ships 16 plugins and none is ReMasker. The repo's plugin_mae.py defines MAEPlugin(ImputerPlugin), named 'mae', and registers it at runtime only, inside its __main__ block. Without a license nothing may be copied verbatim, so the only route is the one BACKLOG I3 already chose: a clean-room PyTorch reimplementation inside the fork, which is MIT-licensed.
cards.api_fit:
The stock class can't be used inside the fork's process. `ReMasker.__init__` calls `get_args_parser().parse_args()` on the trainer's own sys.argv, so argparse exits on TRIDENT's flags. A non-finite loss calls `sys.exit(1)`, which would kill a live run. No seed is set anywhere: RandomSampler has no generator, and torch.rand and parameter initialisation draw from the global stream that the regression fixtures pin. remasker_impute.py also imports hyperimpute at module level, and model_mae.py imports timm's `vision_transformer.Block`.

The reimplementation plugs in as follows:
- **Module.** A new `src/training/remasker_baseline.py` with `RemaskerImputer` (name "remasker"), modelled on `lightgbm_baseline.py`.
- **fit(frame).** Build the vocabulary from `as_category_strings` minus `_NOT_A_CLASS`, so "nan", [MASK] and [NULL] are never classes. Build a float matrix with NaN where `frame.isna()`, as `GradientBoostingImputer._matrix` does. Fit a per-column nanmin/nanmax min-max on the training fold, which is the paper's own normalisation, then train.
- **impute(frame, hidden).** Take `missing = hidden | frame.isna()`, build the NaN matrix without rewriting the frame, run batched inference grouped by observed count (the stock code goes row by row), and invert the min-max. The values come back in the frame's StandardScaler space (data.py:70-73), so no other inverse is needed. Pass observed cells through unchanged, decode categoricals to strings, and `reindex(columns=frame.columns)` so the order check in `score_baselines` passes.
- **Cache.** Register a fourth `_Family("remasker", (imputation_baselines, imputation_metrics, remasker_baseline), ("torch",), fit_remasker_imputers)` in `baseline_cache.py`. The key then carries the torch version and the hostname automatically.
- **Reporting.** Add "remasker" to `EXTERNAL_BASELINES` (summary.py:88). It gets its own gap_to_remasker and stays outside the bar, like missForest (ADR 0017).
- **Determinism.** Wrap fit and impute in `torch.random.fork_rng` with the baseline's own seed. `use_deterministic_algorithms` is process-global, so run ReMasker in the backfill process, not inside a live training run.
- **Backfill.** Drive it through `BaselineScorer(families=...)`, as `scripts/backfill_lgbm_baseline.py:254` does.
cards.categorical_support:
None. model_mae.py's header comment says the implementation supports only numerical values. The paper's mixed tables (Credit Approval, Obesity) enter as scaled numbers. The fork has 13 categorical columns of 20 in credit-g, 36 of 36 in kr-vs-kp and 1 of 8 in electricity (datasets/categorical_columns/*.txt). There are two options, and either is a departure to state:
- **(a) Regress the vocabulary index as a scaled number and round or clip it.** This is the paper's treatment, but ADR 0016:209-210 rejected exactly this for IterativeImputer.
- **(b) One-hot blocks as in KnnImputer, decoded by argmax.** Each block is masked as a unit during training. This is also how DiffPuter encodes categories.

I recommend (b). Report kr-vs-kp, which is all categorical, as outside the method's regime.
cards.feasible_tables:
Run against the stock code's logic (ratio 0.5, batch 64, 600 epochs, a training fold of 70% of the rows), my binomial calculation gives these per-fit crash probabilities from the 0/0 loss:
- **No crash risk on 12 of 21 variants:** all nine 20nan variants, plus credit-g, kr-vs-kp and spambase at 40nan.
- **Crash near-certain (about 1.0 per fit):** credit-g_80, kr-vs-kp_60 and _80, spambase_60 and _80, vehicle_60 and biodeg_60.
- **Crash likely:** credit-g_60 at 0.68 per fit; kc2_60 at 0.12 per fit, which is 0.84 over its 15 fits.

With two fixes, all 21 variants become feasible. First, apply the ratio to each row's observed cells. Second, never feed or target missing cells, and skip an empty loss term. At 60/80nan the result must then be reported as "ReMasker (fixed)", not as the published model.

On the fully numerical tables (spambase, vehicle, biodeg, kc2, pendigits, letter) the method is in its own regime. credit-g, kr-vs-kp and electricity need the categorical departure.

kc2 (365 training rows), vehicle (592) and credit-g (700) sit below the roughly 1,000-row floor that TabImpute's authors give for ReMasker and CACTI. ReMasker's own lead also grows with table size (its Figure 3).

GPU memory is not a constraint: peak use is at most 0.15 GB per fit (CACTI Table A14).
cards.known_failures:
Four failure modes:
- **The 0/0 loss stops training.** When every row in a batch misses at least d - floor(d/2) cells, there is no re-masked cell, the loss is NaN and the code calls sys.exit(1) (remasker-paper.md:113). My calculation for CACTI's 10 tables at MCAR 70% (300 epochs) gives a crash probability of about 1.0 on every one. That matches CACTI's report that ReMasker failed on every MCAR and MNAR dataset at 70% (cacti-paper.md:266). The same calculation gives about 0 for shoppers at 30%, so CACTI's shoppers failures need another cause. This answers part of the Open Question at remasker-paper.md:210, under a binomial approximation.
- **Missing cells are fed as zeros, with no crash.** A row missing more than d/2 cells keeps zero-filled missing cells in the encoder input and in the visible-cell loss, with target 0, which is the column minimum (remasker-paper.md:112). That is 25% of credit-g rows at 40nan and 83-100% of rows at 60/80nan, so a guard on the 0/0 alone is not enough.
- **The masking ratio counts the missing cells,** so the effective re-mask rate falls in rows with gaps (remasker-paper.md:111).
- **The paper's runtime table is not credible.** Table 8 reports a flat 67-74 s from 1k to 20k rows. Two independent measurements of the same code are about 20 times higher: CACTI's per-epoch times (letter 2.10 s/epoch) and DiffPuter's Table 2 (california 1,320 s on an RTX 4090).

Other points:
- **Repo issue #3:** the plugin fails because it loads a hardcoded letter.pt checkpoint.
- **Downstream:** inputs imputed by ReMasker scored below zero filling in MaskTab's Table 5 (masktab-paper.md:318).
- **Mechanisms:** the authors concede that it is weaker under MAR and MNAR (Q2).
- **Benchmark harness:** it amputates at most 8 columns, runs in-sample, and scores AUROC on the same rows it fit (remasker-paper.md:141-146).
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables:
Overlap with the fork's tables is letter and spambase only. ReMasker's "credit" is UCI Credit Approval (690 rows, 15 features; ReMasker_ICLR2024.md:886), not credit-g. kr-vs-kp, vehicle, biodeg, kc2, pendigits and electricity don't appear.

The paper's own numbers are under MAR 30%, in-sample, in min-max space, with at most 8 columns amputated:
- **letter:** RMSE 0.0554 (Table 11, ratio 0.5) and 0.0616 (Table 1 default).
- **spambase:** RMSE 0.0435 in-sample (Table 11) and 0.052 on a held-out half (Table 9).

To put these on the fork's scale, I computed the mean-fill RMSE in min-max space from the fork's _00nan CSVs: 0.154 for letter and 0.057 for spambase. The rough impute_score equivalents are about 0.36-0.40 on letter and 0.77-0.92 on spambase (inferred).

The anchor closest to the fork's protocol comes from DiffPuter's reproduction on letter: MCAR 30%, 70/30 out-of-sample, standardised data, every column amputated. There ReMasker gets RMSE 0.486 (MAE 0.340), which is about 0.49 on impute_score since the mean fill's z-RMSE is near 1 (inferred). The fork's letter_20nan bar is knn10 at 0.473, with TRIDENT at 0.469-0.515 (EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md:557, 646). So expect ReMasker roughly level with knn10 on letter. On spambase_20nan the bar is hgb at 0.865 (EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md:561).

Treat DiffPuter's baseline reproductions with caution: it reports missForest at z-RMSE 0.84 on letter, which is suspiciously bad.
cards.wrapper_effort:
About 17-24 hours, so two to three working days:
- **Model, 3-4 h:** a clean-room model of about 200 lines. The encoder takes the visible tokens only, with a linear value embedding and a fixed sin-cos positional encoding. The decoder has one shared learnable mask token. torch.nn Transformer layers replace timm's Block, which removes the timm dependency.
- **Masking, loss and training loop, 3-4 h:** the two fixes; AdamW (betas 0.9/0.95, weight decay 0.05, base lr 1e-3, 40 warm-up epochs, half-cosine to 1e-5); 600 epochs at batch 64; and batched inference.
- **Adapter, 2 h:** vocabulary, one-hot block encoding and decoding, min-max scaling.
- **Determinism, 2-3 h:** fork_rng, deterministic algorithms, and a reproduction check that a rerun returns the same fill.
- **Tests under strict mypy, 3-4 h.**
- **Cache family, EXTERNAL_BASELINES entry and backfill script, 3-5 h:** the script adapted from backfill_lgbm_baseline.py (387 lines).
- **Smoke test on letter_20nan, 1-2 h:** against the 0.49 anchor.
cards.compute_estimate:
Two independent measurements give about 0.09 s per training row per fit at 600 epochs: CACTI Table A14 (ReMasker, 6/4/32 configuration, letter 2.10 s/epoch, spam 0.58 s/epoch) and DiffPuter Table 2 (california 1,320 s on an RTX 4090). I took 0.09-0.15 s for gorgona8's RTX 3090 Ti.

One fold of each of the 21 variants holds 81,430 training rows. Over 5 folds and 3 seeds that is 1.22M row-fits:
- **Full grid at 600 epochs:** about 30-50 GPU-hours. This agrees with BACKLOG I3's estimate of 40 GPU-hours.
- **Full grid at 300 epochs:** about 15-25 GPU-hours. 300 is the setting CACTI ran.
- **electricity** (31.7k training rows per fold) takes about 40% of the total, 12-20 GPU-hours. letter takes 5-9 and pendigits 3-5.
- **Inference,** row by row at about 2.5 ms per row (CACTI A14), for both populations on every test fold: about 0.5 GPU-hour.

Each fit uses at most 0.15 GB of GPU memory, so about 4 can run at once if TRIDENT isn't using the GPU, for 10-15 hours of wall clock (inferred).

A first slice of the numerical tables at 20/40nan (spambase_20 and _40, vehicle_20, biodeg_20, kc2_20) costs 3-5 GPU-hours. Adding pendigits and letter costs 11-19 GPU-hours.
cards.gap_exposed: RQ1's bar is all trees and KNN: mean_mode, knn5, knn10, hgb, lgbm, with missForest outside it. No published Transformer or masked-autoencoder imputer is scored on the decoder's cells, and that is the same-family comparison a reader asks for after missForest (BACKLOG I3). ReMasker is also the "drop the gap" end of the RQ2 token ladder: one shared mask token, and gaps never enter the encoder.

cards.name: CACTI (Gorla et al., ICML 2025), with CMAE as its no-context ablation
cards.availability: No PyPI package. Code: github.com/sriramlab/CACTI, GPL-3.0, 11 commits, 7 stars. It installs through a conda environment.yml (Python 3.10) plus ucimlrepo 0.0.7, with hyperimpute optional for amputation. Column context needs the Alibaba-NLP/gte-en-mlm-large model, run through tools/precompute_colembed.py. The fork is MIT-licensed, so CACTI's GPL code can't be vendored into it; running it as a subprocess is fine.
cards.api_fit:
CACTI is a command-line tool only. train.py takes --tabular (.tsv or .npz) and --tabular_infer for held-out data. --infer_only with --model_path loads a saved best.pth, and --save_path writes *-predicted.tsv. There is no in-process API.

A BaselineImputer would be a subprocess wrapper:
- **fit:** write the training fold as a TSV with NaN at the gaps, then train into a temporary log directory.
- **impute:** write the test fold with NaN at `hidden | isna` for each population, run --infer_only, read the predictions back, decode the categories, and `reindex(columns=frame.columns)`.

It needs a second environment on gorgona8, beside the fork's uv environment (Python 3.11 or later, torch 2.5.1+cu121). The cache key would also have to carry CACTI's commit and its environment versions, because `_environment_digest` only reads the fork's own module sources and pip versions.

The cheaper route is CMAE: copy masking plus median truncation (Algorithms 1-2, cacti-paper.md:94-108) added as a masking option to the fork's ReMasker reimplementation, with no language model.
cards.categorical_support: Categories go through the same scalar pipeline as numbers, and the paper doesn't say how nominal categories are encoded or decoded (cacti-paper.md:146). The repo README doesn't say either. The fork would face the same choice as for ReMasker: one-hot blocks, or index regression.
cards.feasible_tables:
All 21 variants should run mechanically. Median truncation pads each row up to the batch median, so there is no 0/0 mode, and CACTI itself ran at 70% without failing.

The benefit is the problem. Under MCAR, copy masking reduces to random masking (cacti-paper.md:115), and every one of the fork's E01-E39 variants is MCAR per column. On them CACTI is effectively ReMasker with different hyperparameters.

Context embeddings will add little where column names are cryptic: kr-vs-kp (bkblk, bknwy, ...) and letter and pendigits (inferred). The small tables (kc2, vehicle, credit-g) are below the regime its authors target.
cards.known_failures:
CACTI produced no failures of its own in Appendix D. Points to watch:
- **Defaults:** p_cm = 0.9 was chosen on 4 of the 10 tables, against untuned baselines.
- **Width:** E = 512 collapses (MNAR R² 0.35).
- **Overfitting:** under MAR, test performance overfits after about 300 epochs (Figure 4).
- **Epoch count must be pinned:** the CLI default is 100 epochs, the README examples use 300 and the benchmark script uses 600.
- **Variance:** seed counts are unstated.

The headline MNAR gain over ReMasker comes mostly from ReMasker degrading, not from CACTI improving (cacti-paper.md:253).
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables:
letter and spambase are among CACTI's 10 tables (Table A9). Per-dataset accuracy appears only in figures, and the text has only averages: test R² at 30% MCAR is 0.46 for CACTI against 0.44 for ReMasker (Table 1). "default" is Default of Credit Card Clients, not credit-g.

Runtime per epoch (Table A14, MAR 30%): CACTI 2.95 s on letter and 0.71 s on spam, against ReMasker's 2.10 s and 0.58 s. Peak GPU memory is at most 0.26 GB.
cards.wrapper_effort:
About 14-24 hours as a subprocess family: the environment and model download, the subprocess and TSV glue, checkpoint management for each fold and seed, categorical encoding, establishing determinism (seed control is not documented), the cache key, tests and the backfill.

The CMAE variant, built into the ReMasker reimplementation, costs about 3-5 extra hours.
cards.compute_estimate:
An epoch costs 1.1-1.5 times ReMasker's (Table A14). For the 315 fits:
- **At 300 epochs:** about 20-35 GPU-hours on the 3090 Ti.
- **At 600 epochs:** about 40-70 GPU-hours.

On top of that come one process start per fold and population, and one language-model embedding pass per table, which is small (inferred).
cards.gap_exposed: It is the strongest published Transformer imputer, and its copy masking is aware of the missingness pattern. It is the RQ4 candidate, but the fork's MCAR-only protocol doesn't exercise it.
cards.rq_or_todo:
- RQ1 (thesis-goals.md:75).
- RQ4 copy masking (thesis-goals.md:84, :102).
- Run it after a MAR/MNAR amputation protocol exists in the fork.
cards.reasons:
- The GPL-3.0 license is incompatible with vendoring into the MIT fork.
- It is command-line only, with TSV input and output and a separate Python 3.10 conda environment.
- It needs a language-model download.
- How it encodes categories is undocumented.
- Under the fork's MCAR variants its distinguishing mechanism reduces to ReMasker's random masking, so it would cost 14-24 hours of glue for a near-duplicate result.

The cheap path to its idea is CMAE inside the ReMasker reimplementation, once MAR/MNAR variants exist.
evidence: Wiki references/cacti-paper.md:94-108 (copy masking and median truncation), :115 (reduces to random masking under MCAR), :146 (categories undescribed), :206-219 (Table A9), :253, :258-261, :265-272

cards.name: DiffPuter (Zhang et al., ICLR 2025)
cards.availability: No PyPI package. Code: github.com/hengruizhang98/DiffPuter, MIT, 4 commits, 28 stars, 4 open issues. It installs through a Python 3.12 conda environment plus requirements/diffputer.txt; the paper used PyTorch 1.12.1. The paper is not yet ingested in the wiki: reading-tracker.csv:23 gives relevance 4, not ingested, and todos.md:31 puts it in the next batch.
cards.api_fit:
DiffPuter is a script only: `main.py --dataname X --split_idx k`, hard-wired to the directory layout that download_and_process.py builds for its 9 datasets and 10 masks. The MIT license allows vendoring.

A fork module would need to refactor the script into two calls:
- **fit:** EM on the training fold, with about 4-5 rounds of training the diffusion MLP and then an E-step.
- **impute:** the paper's single out-of-sample E-step on the test fold (50 sampling steps, 10 samples per cell, averaged), with NaN at `hidden | isna`.

The data handling matches the fork's. DiffPuter standardises numerical columns, which is the fork's z-space, and one-hots categorical columns, which is KnnImputer's encoding, decoded by argmax. Sampling is stochastic, so it needs a seeded generator under `fork_rng`. It would join the cache as a family of its own, with libraries=("torch",).
cards.categorical_support: Yes, coarsely. Discrete columns are one-hot encoded as 0/1, treated as continuous and standardised, and discrete imputation is scored by accuracy. That makes it compatible with credit-g, kr-vs-kp and electricity without a new departure.
cards.feasible_tables:
All 21 variants should run in principle: EM starts from the column mean, so there is no 0/0 mode. Three things are untested:
- **Small tables:** TabImpute's authors dropped DiffPuter because it "did not converge well" on tables of at most 235 rows (tabimpute-paper.md:128). kc2 (365 training rows), vehicle (592) and credit-g (700) are larger but still untested.
- **High missingness:** the paper's main results are at 30%. CACTI ran DiffPuter at 70% and it worked.
- **Memory:** not a concern, with a 1024-wide MLP on a 24 GB GPU.
cards.known_failures:
- **NaN losses:** DiffPuter failed on shoppers at 30% under all three mechanisms in CACTI's runs (cacti-paper.md:265-270).
- **Non-convergence:** on tiny tables (TabImpute).
- **Under MNAR:** its R² dropped from 0.42-0.43 to 0.37 (cacti-paper.md:253).
- **The paper's dataset count:** it says ten datasets but lists nine.
- **Its baseline reproductions look weak:** missForest at z-RMSE 0.84 on letter.
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables:
letter only. spambase, credit-g and the other fork tables are absent.

On letter at MCAR 30%, 70/30 out-of-sample, on standardised data: DiffPuter RMSE 0.477 (MAE 0.307), against ReMasker's 0.486 (0.340). Under MAR, in-sample: DiffPuter 0.481, ReMasker 0.480, HyperImpute 0.575, missForest 0.842.

The fork's letter_20nan bar is knn10 at 0.473 (EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md:557), so DiffPuter would likely land roughly level with it (inferred).
cards.wrapper_effort: About 16-28 hours: refactor main.py into fit and impute and strip out its dataset loader; keep each one-hot block hidden as a unit; seed the sampling and check determinism; tests; the cache family; the backfill.
cards.compute_estimate:
Its Table 2 on an RTX 4090 gives 1,927 s for California (about 14.4k training rows) and 2,143 s for Adult (about 22.8k). That is a large fixed cost with weak dependence on size, so about 1,000-2,500 s per fit.
- **Full grid of 315 fits:** about 100-200 GPU-hours, more on the 3090 Ti (inferred).
- **The three large 20nan tables only** (pendigits, letter, electricity, 45 fits): about 15-30 GPU-hours.
cards.gap_exposed: RQ1 has no generative imputer: diffusion with EM, not a Transformer. It would test distributional fit against point accuracy. The wiki's tracker comment notes that a Transformer denoiser inside EM is an open gap.

- Ingest it first: reading-tracker.csv:23 and todos.md:31 (t13's next batch).

cards.name: LightGBM, native NaN handling (MIA-style learned split direction)
cards.availability: Already a dependency: lightgbm 4.7.0 (pyproject.toml 'lightgbm>=4.7', uv.lock:1349-1350), MIT license, installed in .venv. The fork already uses it for the lgbm imputer (src/training/lightgbm_baseline.py:44-58).
cards.api_fit: Uses the classification folds, not the BaselineImputer protocol. LGBMClassifier is fit on X[train]; early stopping on X[validation] (callbacks=[early_stopping(50)], logloss), which mirrors TRIDENT keeping its best validation-loss epoch (finetuning.py:174-181). Then predict test and call build_fold_result. Use class_weight='balanced' to mirror TRIDENT's balanced cross-entropy weights (finetuning.py:91-100); pre-register that and report unweighted as a sensitivity check. Set deterministic=True, force_row_wise=True, fixed n_jobs and random_state=seed (as lightgbm_baseline.py:50-55). Numerics go in as they are (scaled, NaN kept). Categoricals go in as training-fold vocabulary codes with NaN for missing or unseen values, as in GradientBoostingImputer._matrix (imputation_baselines.py:277-293), passed via categorical_feature, or as pandas 'category' dtype. Do not feed as_category_strings output to a native arm: it renders NaN as the string 'nan' (embedder.py:17-27; MISSING_MARKER at imputation_baselines.py:33), which turns missingness into a category (the BACKLOG C2 pattern).
cards.categorical_support: Native via categorical_feature; cardinality is at most 10 here; the all-categorical kr-vs-kp is fine. Missing values follow a learned split direction.
cards.feasible_tables: All 45 variants. No GPU needed.
cards.known_failures: letter has 26 classes, so 26 trees per round; it is the slowest table. kc2 validation folds hold about 52 rows, so early stopping there is noisy; use a patience and a minimum number of rounds. No failures in the fork's existing LightGBM use (ADR 0017 bar).
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: TRIDENT Table 3, LightGBM mean macro-F1 over the 9 tables: 0.8494 / 0.8324 / 0.7280 / 0.6902 / 0.5467 at 0/20/40/60/80%. That is one 80/10/10 split at seed 42, tuned with 20 Optuna trials on validation F1. LightGBM is best at 0-20%. Figure 3: LightGBM and XGBoost are at or above TRIDENT on electricity and letter at every level (Wiki/references/trident-paper.md:149-170). SAINT paper: spambase LightGBM AUROC 99.01 (different metric; Wiki/references/saint-paper.md:156).
cards.wrapper_effort: About 1 h on top of the harness: build the matrix, train with early stopping, predict.
cards.compute_estimate: Anchor from ADR 0016's timing table (gorgona8, 8 threads): one default LightGBM model on 14k-32k rows takes about 0.14-0.25 s; letter's multiclass model is about 26x that, roughly 3-4 s. 675 fold cells (45 variants x 15 fold pairs) is 10-30 CPU-minutes at defaults and about 1 CPU-hour with early stopping up to 2000 rounds. The Windows box (12 logical cores) is enough.

cards.name: Mean/mode imputation + missing indicator + GBDT
cards.availability: In the fork: MeanModeImputer (src/training/imputation_baselines.py:79-101), which follows the BaselineImputer protocol (imputation_baselines.py:54-69). sklearn 1.9 SimpleImputer(add_indicator=True) is also available (checked).
cards.api_fit: Per fold: MeanModeImputer.fit on the training rows' features. Then impute(part, hidden=np.zeros(shape, bool)) on train, validation and test; it returns floats in scaled space and category strings, with no NaN left. Append 0/1 indicators from part.isna() for the columns that have gaps in the training fold, then train the learners from the LightGBM, XGBoost and HGB cards. Impute before the GBDT; otherwise the arm is just native GBDT plus indicators.
cards.categorical_support: Mode fill on the training-fold vocabulary; the GBDT then sees complete categories.
cards.feasible_tables: The 36 variants with gaps. On 00nan the arm is identical to native GBDT.
cards.known_failures: The gaps are MCAR by construction: generate_splits.py:26-50 hides cells per column independently of y and of the values. So the indicators carry no label information on these tables, and the expected indicator gain is about 0, apart from capacity effects. Indicators double the width (spambase 57 -> 114). At 80%, columns become mostly constant fills.
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: None on these tables. TRIDENT's paper imputed RF and the deep baselines with mode + a LightGBM imputer and no indicator (Wiki/references/trident-paper.md:209). On natural health missingness, constant fill + indicator ran close behind GBDT-MIA (Wiki/projects/trident/thesis-goals.md:140).
cards.wrapper_effort: About 1 h.
cards.compute_estimate: Imputation is trivial. The GBDTs cost about 2x the native arm because of the doubled width: roughly 1 CPU-hour for 540 fold cells x 3 learners.
cards.gap_exposed: The 'imputation + indicator' side of t1 on classification. On MCAR it is a calibration arm (it should tie with native) before the MNAR and clinical tables.

cards.name: Producing TRIDENT classification runs on the same folds (step zero, tier 1: defaults)
cards.availability: In the fork. Classification is the default task (types.py:83; --task at config.py:454-465). The fine-tuning stage is train_and_evaluate_classifier (runner.py:168-176).
cards.api_fit: CLI: `uv run --python 3.11 python main.py --dataset_name <variant> --cv_folds 5 --seed <s>` (--task classification is optional because it is the default). `--all --nan_level N --cv_folds 5 --seed s` sweeps one level (main.py run_all; config.py:315-327), but can't be combined with --use_optuna (config.py:250-251). Better: clone scripts/experiments/confirmatory_run.py with Namespace(task='classification', cv_folds=5, mlflow_tags={'experiment': ...}) and run_confirmatory_queue.sh (4 concurrent queues, thread caps, resumable, a cutoff) on gorgona8, which is the store writer. Hyperparameters: no classification config exists. datasets/hiperparams/* holds only *.imputation.json, and classification never reads those, so _load_base_hyperparameters falls through to 'defaults' (config.py:94-116). Those are the dataclass defaults (types.py:195-212: DIM 128, HEADS 16, LAYERS 2, DIM_FEED 32, DROPOUT 0.2, EPOCHS_PRE 300, EPOCH_FINE 150, BATCH 256, LR_PRE 3.4e-4, LR_FINE 1e-3, PROB_MASCARA 0.5), with the 'embedding' pre-training objective (types.py:29) and the cosine_legacy schedule (types.py:18). cosine_legacy is B1's full-cosine-cycle bug, kept as the classification default (BACKLOG.md:14). Pre-register whether to pass --lr_scheduler cosine. The paper's tuned values were never released (t11).

cards.name: Equal-budget HPO on validation for both sides (TabZilla style, 20 trials)
cards.availability: optuna 4.9.0 is locked (uv.lock:2154-2155). TabZilla used at most 30 settings (1 default plus 29 random, via Optuna) on 10 OpenML folds, selected on validation, with a 10 h limit (https://arxiv.org/html/2305.02997v4). TRIDENT's paper gave its baselines 20 Optuna trials of 50 epochs, ranked on validation F1 (Wiki/entities/tabzilla.md:38).
cards.api_fit: GBDT side: one study per (variant, seed, fold), TPE seeded by the run seed, 20 trials, ranked by macro-F1 on fold.validation_indices, best configuration scored on test. TRIDENT side: opt.py's classification objective is test macro-F1 on the predefined split. Trial args never set cv_folds (opt.py:210-238), so build_folds reads the split JSON (data.py:186-201). search_objective='f1_macro' (opt.py:175-179) is read from the returned test metrics (opt.py:285), and FoldResult carries test metrics only (finetuning.py:186-192). Validation macro-F1 exists only as a per-epoch log (finetuning.py:163-168). Needed changes: return the validation macro-F1 at the kept epoch (the imputation side does this through score_search_objective, opt.py:233), rank trials by it, and tune on a split whose validation rows aren't test rows of the CV folds being scored.
cards.categorical_support: Not applicable.
cards.feasible_tables: GBDTs: all 45 variants, tuned per fold. TRIDENT tuned per fold is infeasible (675 x 20 = 13,500 trainings); tuned once per variant (45 x 20) it is feasible.
cards.known_failures: The classification search space trains 20-60 pre-training and 20-60 fine-tuning epochs (opt.py:134, 156-158) against the defaults of 300/150, so a tuned TRIDENT may be weaker than the defaults. Tuning once per variant and applying the result to all 15 folds leaks mild selection information into folds whose test rows overlap the tuning validation set; use the same protocol for the GBDTs to keep it symmetric. opt.py has its own mypy relaxation block (pyproject.toml), so changing it touches the typing ramp.
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: Table 3's baseline numbers are TabZilla-tuned on validation; TRIDENT's were tuned on test (Wiki/references/trident-paper.md:206).
cards.wrapper_effort: GBDT side 2-3 h. TRIDENT side 4-8 h: change the opt.py objective, add the validation readout, add tests.
cards.compute_estimate: GBDTs: 675 fold cells x 3 learners x 20 trials is about 40k fits, roughly 10-30 CPU-hours; about 1-2 h of wall time on gorgona8's 32 cores. TRIDENT tuned per variant: 45 x 20 short trials (each about 0.1-0.2 of a default fold), about 100-180 default-fold equivalents, adding 15-25% to the tier-1 GPU time. TRIDENT tuned per fold: 100+ GPU-hours.
cards.gap_exposed: Removes the asymmetry in which the paper's TRIDENT was tuned on test and the baselines on validation (owner-confirmed; Wiki/hot.md:23). Speaks to TabZilla's finding that light GBDT tuning can matter more than which model family you pick.

cards.reasons: The GBDT half is quick. The TRIDENT half needs an opt.py change, a decision about which split to tune on, and tens of GPU-hours or more. Run tier 1 (defaults on both sides) first.

cards.name: Classification-baseline harness on the fork's folds (needed by every card below)
cards.availability: Nothing to install: it is built from the fork's own code. The fork has no protocol for classifier baselines (BaselineImputer, fork:src/training/imputation_baselines.py:54-68, covers imputation only) and has never made a classification run.
cards.api_fit: For each variant and seed, call prepare_dataset (fork:src/training/data.py:47-87) and build_folds(frame, label, cv_folds=5, seed) (data.py:182-260). Train on fold.train_indices, tune and early-stop on fold.validation_indices (10% of rows; validation_ratio, data.py:226), and score fold.test_indices with build_fold_result (fork:src/training/finetuning.py:19-61), so macro-F1 is computed exactly as TRIDENT's is. VERIFIED: the folds depend only on labels, row count, cv_folds and seed (data.py:214-259). The labels are the same in every _XXnan file: generate_splits.py never masks 'class', and I checked credit-g, electricity and letter, 00nan against 80nan. So one seed gives identical folds at all 5 levels and for TRIDENT, and the pairing is exact. What the data look like on arrival: features standardized on the WHOLE table before the folds are cut (data.py:69-73), labels encoded on the whole table (data.py:60-61), categoricals as raw strings (electricity's day is spelled '3.0', data.py:124-140), gaps as NaN (the [NULL] string is substituted only inside the TRIDENT path). What every wrapper needs: (1) a vocabulary built per fold, with a reserved index for missing and unseen values; (2) for models with no NaN path, numerical gaps filled and an indicator added; the fork's MeanModeImputer and LightGbmImputer (lightgbm_baseline.py) can be reused for this, and it is the t3 arm; (3) balanced class weights, to match TRIDENT (finetuning.py:91-99), or a stated deviation. Per-fold results go to a CSV. MLflow writes happen only on gorgona8 (fork:AGENTS.md:9).
cards.categorical_support: Not applicable: the harness supplies the wrappers with ordinal codes plus a missing index.
cards.feasible_tables: All 45 classification variants exist on disk (9 tables x 00/20/40/60/80nan, datasets/processed_datasets/*). That is more than the 21 imputation variants.
cards.known_failures: In the fork's Optuna mode, classification trials still seem to be ranked on test f1_macro: opt.py:174-179 says only imputation was moved to validation (ADR 0005). This is the upstream defect described at wiki:references/trident-paper.md:206, and it must be fixed before step zero can claim equal HPO. Any new code in scripts/ or src/ falls under the strict mypy gate (fork:AGENTS.md:11), so untyped libraries (rtdl, pytorch_tabnet, vendored SAINT/NAIM) need ignore_missing_imports or ramp blocks in pyproject.toml.

cards.wrapper_effort: 6-10 h: loader, per-fold encoding, the fold and seed loop, CSV logging, 2-3 unit tests and typing. Paid once and shared by every method card.

cards.name: FT-Transformer via rtdl_revisiting_models
cards.availability: pip install rtdl_revisiting_models (0.0.2, 2023-11-30, Apache-2.0, requires torch>=1.8,<3). It fits the fork's venv as locked: Python>=3.11, torch 2.5.1+cu121, numpy 2.4.6, scikit-learn 1.9.0 (uv.lock). The repo, yandex-research/rtdl-revisiting-models, is not archived; last push 2024-11-12. The package has model classes only, no training loop. It replaces the old 'rtdl' 0.0.13 that TabZilla pins. https://pypi.org/project/rtdl-revisiting-models/
cards.api_fit: Classification folds only. Build FTTransformer(n_cont_features, cat_cardinalities, d_out=n_classes, **FTTransformer.get_default_kwargs()), then call forward(x_cont float, x_cat int64). Numerical gaps: fill with the training mean of the fold (the frame is already z-scored, so about 0) or with the fork's LightGbmImputer, and append a per-column missing indicator to x_cont. Categorical gaps: one extra index per column in cat_cardinalities. Training loop: make_default_optimizer (AdamW), batch 256-512, early stopping on the fold's validation split.
cards.categorical_support: Native, through cat_cardinalities with ordinal int64 codes. A missing categorical becomes an extra category, which acts as a learned per-column missing embedding for categorical columns only. Numerical gaps have no native path.
cards.feasible_tables: All 9 tables, all 45 variants. The widest is spambase (57 features plus CLS), well within memory. Electricity (45k rows) and letter (20k) dominate the time.
cards.known_failures: In TRIDENT's Table 3 (TabZilla, rtdl 0.0.13 make_default, imputed inputs), FT-T is the weakest deep baseline: 0.7347 at 0%, 0.4500 at 80%. In Figure 3 it is flat at about 0.41 on credit-g and about 0.44 on kc2, which look like single-class predictions (wiki:references/trident-paper.md:171). In NAIM's untuned benchmark, FT-T + KNN was well below Random Forest even on clean data (wiki:references/naim-paper.md:318). Check every fold for degenerate predictions.
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: TRIDENT Table 3, means over these 9 tables: 0.7347 / 0.7137 / 0.6882 / 0.5880 / 0.4500 at 0/20/40/60/80% (trident-paper.md:151-157). Protocol differs: one 80/10/10 split, seed 42, mode + LightGBM imputation, TabZilla HPO. NAIM Table C.8 has FT-T + mean/KNN/MICE on spambase, but as AUC on NAIM's own MCAR grid. I found no per-dataset macro-F1 under the fork's protocol.
cards.wrapper_effort: 3-5 h on top of the shared harness: training loop, early stopping, indicator block, tests.
cards.compute_estimate: Inferred, not measured. Assumes one RTX 3090 Ti and about half the fork's TRIDENT fine-tuning throughput (about 30k rows/s, from fork:docs/tickets/0003-training-loop-performance.md:69-74). Default config (3 blocks, d_token 192), about 100 epochs with early stopping: about 3 GPU-h per seed (225 fits), 8-10 h for all 675. With the paper's HPO budget (20 trials x 50 epochs per model and variant, trident-paper.md:206), tuning once per variant adds about 5 h. Tuning per fold and seed multiplies that by 15 (about 80 h), which does not fit in a day.
cards.gap_exposed: Table 3's deep baselines have never been run with repeated splits, equal HPO or a missing indicator.
cards.rq_or_todo: t3; step zero; the RQ2 bar (imputation + indicator on a Transformer backbone).
cards.reasons: pip-installable into the existing venv with no conflicts, and model-only, so it is a small training loop. All 45 variants at default hyperparameters fit in under a day on one GPU. Assumes the shared harness exists.
evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yandex-research/rtdl-revisiting-models/main/package/README.md (model classes only, forward(x_cont, x_cat), integer codes)

cards.name: TabNet via pytorch-tabnet
cards.availability: pip install pytorch-tabnet (4.1.0, 2023-07-23; needs torch>=1.3, numpy>=1.17, scikit_learn>0.21). The repo, dreamquark-ai/tabnet, is MIT on GitHub, though PyPI's license field is empty; not archived, last push 2024-10-23, 68 open issues. TabZilla pins 3.1.1. Whether 4.1.0 works with the fork's numpy 2.4.6, scikit-learn 1.9.0 and torch 2.5.1 is UNVERIFIED: the release predates numpy 2.
cards.api_fit: Classification folds. TabNetClassifier(cat_idxs, cat_dims, cat_emb_dim).fit(X_train, y_train, eval_set=[(X_val, y_val)], patience, max_epochs) on numpy arrays, with an sklearn-like predict. check_input calls sklearn check_array(X, accept_sparse=True), and its default rejects NaN. So, as for FT-T, numerical gaps must be filled with an indicator added, and categoricals coded with a missing index.
cards.categorical_support: Native embeddings through cat_idxs/cat_dims; a missing value is an extra category index.
cards.feasible_tables: All 9 tables, all 45 variants.
cards.known_failures: Table 3 (imputed inputs): 0.7881 at 0%, 0.4668 at 80%. The numpy 2 compatibility is unverified. If it breaks, use pytorch-tabular's TabNet or a separate venv.
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: TRIDENT Table 3 TabNet row: 0.7881 / 0.7245 / 0.6717 / 0.6144 / 0.4668 (trident-paper.md:151-157; one split, imputed). NAIM Table C.8 has TabNet + KNN on spambase, as AUC on NAIM's own grid.
cards.wrapper_effort: 2-3 h: the estimator already has early stopping and eval sets.
cards.compute_estimate: Inferred. Defaults (n_d = n_a = 8, batch 1024, virtual batch 128), 100-200 epochs, patience 15: about 2-4 GPU-h per seed, 6-12 h for 675 fits. The six small tables can run on CPU in parallel. One HPO pass per variant adds about one seed's worth.
cards.gap_exposed: Same as FT-T: no repeated-split, equal-HPO, indicator-aware TabNet baseline exists.
cards.rq_or_todo: t3; step zero.
cards.reasons: pip-installable, with a fit/predict API that maps straight onto train/val/test indices, and small compute. The one open risk is numpy 2 compatibility, and pytorch-tabular is the fallback.

cards.name: TabNet + FT-Transformer via pytorch-tabular (one-package alternative)
cards.availability: pip install pytorch-tabular (1.2.0, 2026-01-26, MIT; Python >=3.10,<3.15; torch>=1.11; pytorch-lightning>=2.0,<2.7). The repo, manujosephv/pytorch_tabular, is active (pushed 2026-10-13). Models include TabNet, FT Transformer, TabTransformer, GATE, GANDALF, DANet, NODE, AutoInt and CategoryEmbedding. No SAINT, no NAIM.
cards.api_fit: Classification folds. TabularModel(data_config, model_config, optimizer_config, trainer_config).fit(train=df, validation=df), then predict(test_df), which takes the fork's DataFrames directly. With handle_missing_values=True (the default), categorical NaN is treated as unknown. Continuous NaN handling is undocumented, so fill and add an indicator first. It normalizes continuous columns itself, so set that off or accept a second scaling on top of the fork's z-scores.
cards.categorical_support: Native embeddings; NaN becomes the unknown category.
cards.feasible_tables: All 9 tables, all 45 variants.
cards.known_failures: Lightning adds per-run overhead and its own checkpoints and loggers. Its TabNet differs from the pytorch-tabnet estimator TabZilla used, so numbers will move against Table 3.
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: Same as the FT-T and TabNet cards (TRIDENT Table 3). None from pytorch-tabular itself.
cards.wrapper_effort: 3-5 h covers both models (one DataConfig). Adds pytorch-lightning to the fork's uv.lock, or needs a second venv.
cards.compute_estimate: Inferred: about 1.2-1.5x the direct-library estimates because of Lightning overhead, so about 10-15 h for 675 fits of each model at defaults.
cards.gap_exposed: Same as FT-T and TabNet.
cards.rq_or_todo: t3; step zero.
cards.reasons: Use it only if pytorch-tabnet fails under numpy 2. Otherwise the two direct libraries are lighter dependencies and closer to the implementations TabZilla wrapped.

cards.name: TabZilla (the TRIDENT paper's harness)
cards.availability: Not on PyPI. github.com/naszilla/tabzilla, Apache-2.0, 433 commits, last commit 2024-03-22. Needs its own Python 3.10 venv from TabZilla/pip_requirements.txt: torch==1.13.1, rtdl==0.0.13, pytorch-tabnet==3.1.1, optuna==3.2.0, numpy 1.25.1, scikit-learn 1.3.0. Incompatible with the fork's venv (Python >=3.11, torch 2.5.1, numpy 2.4.6).
cards.api_fit: Classification only. Datasets come from OpenML tasks, with OpenML's 10-fold splits; each fold's validation set is the next fold's test set (tabzilla_preprocessors_openml.py), a different protocol from build_folds. process_data accepts arbitrary train/val/test index arrays, so the fork's folds could be injected, but through a custom preprocessor for each of the 45 local CSVs. Default preprocessing fills numerical gaps with SimpleImputer() (mean), fitted on train. TRIDENT replaced it with mode + LightGBM (trident-paper.md:209), which would have to be re-added.
cards.categorical_support: cat_idx/cat_dims are passed to the models. process_data leaves categorical NaN unimputed; what happens downstream is unverified.
cards.feasible_tables: All 45 in principle.
cards.known_failures: Its SAINT wrapper builds every mask as np.ones_like(X), so SAINT never uses its missing token (this is why TRIDENT's SAINT was 'SAINT on imputed data'). The wrapper also hard-codes lr=3e-5 and switches to dim 8 and batch 64 when a table has 50 or more features (spambase has 57). TRIDENT's TabZilla runs gave degenerate FT-T on credit-g and kc2, and SAINT at about 0.10 on vehicle at 0% and 60% (trident-paper.md:171).
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: TRIDENT Table 3: all three deep baselines on all 9 tables at 5 levels, run with TabZilla (trident-paper.md:151-157). A secondary source says TabZilla's own 176-dataset metadataset includes credit-g (OpenML 31); I found no per-dataset numbers.
cards.wrapper_effort: 2-3 days: a second venv, a preprocessor for 45 variants with injected folds, the paper's imputer, result parsing. Read define_trial_parameters for the 'TabZilla defaults' search spaces the paper cites; running the harness isn't worth it.
cards.compute_estimate: Same models as the FT-T, TabNet and SAINT cards, plus TabZilla's HPO. Not cheaper than calling the libraries directly.
cards.gap_exposed: Only an exact replay of Table 3's own protocol (one split, imputed SAINT), which is what step zero sets out to replace.
cards.rq_or_todo: Step zero; t3 (as a reference for search spaces only).
cards.reasons: Not pip-installable; old pinned stack; OpenML-task splits that don't match the fork's folds; and its SAINT bypasses native missing handling. The underlying libraries can be called directly in the fork's venv for a fraction of the effort.
evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/naszilla/tabzilla/main/TabZilla/models/saint.py (mask = np.ones_like(X); lr 0.00003; dim 8 / batch 64 if >=50 features)
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/naszilla/tabzilla/main/TabZilla/tabzilla_preprocessors_openml.py (OpenML task splits; val = next fold's test)

cards.name: Native SAINT (official somepago/saint code, vendored; marineLM MySAINT as a numerical-only pilot)
cards.availability: No pip package implements native SAINT (see the next card). (a) Official code at github.com/somepago/saint: Apache-2.0, 14 commits, last commit 2021-12-06, archived read-only on 2026-03-11, 15 open issues. Its environment is Python 3.8.10, torch 1.8.1/cu111, numpy 1.20.2 (saint_environment.yml). (b) marineLM/Imputation_for_prediction_benchmark, python/saint/ (BSD-3; model.py, pretrainmodel.py, my_saint.py). Its MySAINT (about 113 lines) wraps the vendored SAINT model and passes NaN masks natively. It is the code behind the native-SAINT results in Le Morvan & Varoquaux (ICLR 2025).
cards.api_fit: Classification folds. The official data_prep_openml(ds_id, ...) downloads by OpenML ID and makes a random, unstratified 65/15/20 split. It must be rewritten to take the fork's frame and build_folds' positional indices; data_split and DataSetCatCon already accept any arrays plus a mask (1 = observed). Pass the real NaN mask to embed_data_mask, not ones: it overwrites masked cells with the per-feature rows of mask_embeds_cont and mask_embeds_cat. Fill continuous gaps with 0 (the frame is already z-scored) instead of the official fill. Contrastive + denoising pre-training (pretraining.py) is optional; report whether it was used, since its denoising loss targets placeholders. The same code with an all-ones mask reproduces the paper's 'SAINT on imputed data' arm, so one implementation covers both.
cards.categorical_support: Official code: yes. Categoricals are embedded with a 'MissingValue' category, and the mask embedding then overrides it. MySAINT: none ('no categorical data for now', categories=tuple([1])), and its head is regression-first (y.squeeze() caveat), so multiclass use (vehicle 4 classes, pendigits 10, letter 26) is unverified.
cards.feasible_tables: Official code: all 9 tables and 45 variants. With at most 57 features, the intersample row width (n+1)*d stays small (about 1.9k at d=32 on spambase). MySAINT pilot: only the 6 all-numerical tables (vehicle, biodeg, kc2, spambase, pendigits, letter: 30 variants). Electricity would need its single categorical, day, treated as numeric, which is a deviation.
cards.known_failures: From the wiki's SAINT page: :93, every continuous gap gets the training mean of one arbitrary column, and that value enters the normalization stats; :97, the denoising loss targets the placeholder at missing cells; :98, old_version resets the val/test masks to ones when --train_mask_prob is 0 (use main, not old_version); :176, SAINT-i collapses at 70-90% MCAR (use full SAINT); :86, predictions depend on the batch. Code issues: mixup_data hard-codes .cuda(), and np.arange gives int32 on Windows with numpy<2. Compatibility with torch 2.5 and numpy 2 is unverified. In Le Morvan & Varoquaux, native SAINT ranked below missforest + SAINT + indicator in all four settings (wiki:projects/trident/thesis-goals.md:140).
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: SAINT paper, Appendix Table 7: spambase AUROC 98.54 for SAINT vs 99.01 for LightGBM, on complete data with a random 65/15/20 split and 5 trials (wiki:references/saint-paper.md:156). TRIDENT Table 3, SAINT on imputed inputs: 0.7658 / 0.7676 / 0.7042 / 0.6167 / 0.4991 (trident-paper.md:153-157).
cards.wrapper_effort: 10-16 h with the official code: loader rewrite, mask plumbing, fill fix, CPU/GPU fixes, supervised and optional pre-training paths, and a parity check on one OpenML dataset against the original script. 3-5 h for a MySAINT pilot on the numerical tables only.
cards.compute_estimate: Inferred. With Le Morvan's defaults (depth 1, 4 heads, dim 32, batch 256, 100 epochs, lr 1e-4, AdamW with weight decay 0.01, early stopping), supervised training takes about 2-4 GPU-h per seed and 6-12 h for 675 fits. Pre-training roughly doubles that. For scale, SAINT's own paper reports about 4 GPU-days on a 2080 Ti for all of its experiments.
cards.gap_exposed: TRIDENT has never been compared with the per-column missing token that predates it (SAINT, Appendix B). Its Section 4.2 claim that SAINT can't handle missing values was never tested (trident-paper.md:212).
cards.rq_or_todo: RQ2 arm: a per-column token on a different backbone (thesis-goals.md:142); t3; positioning (projects/trident/trident#Positioning).
cards.reasons: Native SAINT exists only in research code: one archived repo on a 2021 stack, and one numerical-only wrapper. Vendoring it and getting the mask plumbing and fill right takes 1.5-2 days. Compute is not the constraint.
evidence: https://github.com/somepago/saint (Apache-2.0, archived 2026-03-11, python 3.8, OpenML IDs only)

cards.name: SAINT from pip packages (pytorch-widedeep, DeepTab, TALENT): none is native
cards.availability: pytorch-widedeep 1.7.0 (2025-09-27, MIT, torch>=2.0) exports SAINT, FTTransformer and TabNet. deeptab 2.0.0 (2026-06-24, MIT, torch>=2.2.2,<2.10, lightning, pretab<0.0.2) has SAINT and FTTransformer. TALENT (MIT, installable only via pip install git+...) has SAINT, FT-T and TabNet.
cards.api_fit: None of them passes a missing mask to SAINT. pytorch-widedeep's SAINT.forward(X) takes a single tensor with no mask. deeptab's architectures/saint.py has no mask or missing-value code, and its preprocessing (PreTab) imputes. TALENT imputes before the model (num_nan_policy mean|median, cat_nan_policy new|most_frequent) and expects N_/C_/y_ train/val/test .npy files for every split. So all three give SAINT on imputed inputs, which is what TRIDENT already ran.
cards.categorical_support: Yes in all three, through their own encoders, with no missing token.
cards.feasible_tables: All 45 for an imputed-SAINT arm.
cards.known_failures: These are reimplementations, so their numbers aren't comparable to the official code. For TALENT, the 45 variants x 15 fold pairs would each need their own exported .npy files.
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: None found.
cards.wrapper_effort: 2-4 h for an imputed-SAINT arm through deeptab or pytorch-widedeep. Native SAINT isn't reachable through these packages at any effort.
cards.compute_estimate: Similar to the official code: about 2-4 GPU-h per seed at defaults (inferred).
cards.gap_exposed: Nothing beyond what TRIDENT already did.
cards.rq_or_todo: t3, only if an imputed-SAINT arm is wanted next to native SAINT.
cards.reasons: The question asked was whether any package gives native SAINT, and none does. For the imputed arm, the vendored official code with an all-ones mask is the more faithful choice anyway.

cards.name: NAIM (cosbidev/NAIM, model vendored into the fork's loop)
cards.availability: No pip package. github.com/cosbidev/NAIM: MIT, 11 commits, last commit 2026-03-14 (README only). Requirements: Python 3.9, torch==1.13.0. The pipeline is driven by Hydra, has its own CV, and ships its own baselines (AdaBoost, DT, FT-Transformer, HGB, MLP, RF, SVM, TabNet, TabTransformer, XGBoost; simple, kNN and iterative imputers). A 'predefined' CV config exists (idxs: [-100,-1]), but its format is undocumented, so don't rely on it.
cards.api_fit: Classification folds. Vendor CMC_utils/models/tabular/naim/naim.py (about 300 lines, torch only) and tabular_tokenizer.py, and skip the Hydra pipeline. NAIM(input_size, output_size, cat_idxs, cat_dims, d_token, embedder_initialization, bias, mask_type, missing_value, ...) takes one float tensor with NaN at the gaps. Categoricals arrive as integer codes, and NaN maps to the padding index cat_dims[j]; numerical NaN becomes 0 plus an attention mask. That matches the fork's frames almost one to one: per-fold codes, NaN kept as is. Port two things from the repo: the feature-drop augmentation (CMC_utils/data_augmentation/tabular.py) and the training recipe (Adam, cross-entropy, L1+L2, learning rate divided by 10 after 25 stagnant epochs, early stopping with patience 50 after 50 warm-up epochs; config mask_type 2, bias False, d_token 6, 6 layers, 3 heads, feed-forward 1000).
cards.categorical_support: Native: each feature has its own lookup table, with a frozen zero padding row for missing.
cards.feasible_tables: All 45 with a capped recipe. With the paper's recipe, only the 6 small tables (4.6k rows or fewer) fit in a day.
cards.known_failures: From the wiki's NAIM page: :141, missing positions still reach the linear head as a learned constant, an implicit indicator; :143, the code draws c from {1..v-2} and augments only rows with more than 2 observed features (the paper says v-1); :322, a zero numerical embedding isn't unique to missing values. In the fork's z-scored frame, x=0 is each column's mean, so only the attention mask separates 'missing' from 'at the mean'. :323, the first attention layer may not see numerical values. The defaults are untuned: d_e = 6, with 2-dimensional heads. Whether naim.py runs on torch 2.5 is unverified.
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: Spambase is in NAIM's benchmark. At 0/0, NAIM's AUC is 98.50 vs 98.73 for XGBoost, and NAIM is best in only 4 of 36 spambase cells (wiki:references/naim-paper.md:271-273). These are AUCs on NAIM's train x test MCAR grid (0/5/10/25/50/75%) with 5-fold stratified CV, so a sanity anchor only.
cards.wrapper_effort: 6-10 h: vendoring, a typing ramp block, the training loop, feature drop, and tests.
cards.compute_estimate: Inferred. With the paper's recipe (batch 32, up to 1500 epochs, at least 100 by construction), electricity takes about 990 steps per epoch, or about 15-40 min per fit: roughly 40-70 GPU-h for 675 fits. A capped recipe (batch 256, at most 300 epochs, patience 20) needs about 6-12 h; the cap must be reported as a deviation.
cards.gap_exposed: The fixed-zero, hard-mask design against TRIDENT's learned, attended [NULL] token: the opposite bet on what a missing token should carry (naim-paper.md:156).
cards.rq_or_todo: Baselines list (thesis-goals.md:147); RQ2 arm, zero + hard mask (thesis-goals.md:150).
cards.reasons: The code is public, small and NaN-native, so it maps cleanly onto the fork's folds. But it is not a package, the training recipe and feature drop have to be ported, and the paper's batch-32 recipe is too slow on electricity and letter without a declared cap.

cards.name: TRIDENT 'no pre-training + random feature drop' control
cards.availability: Inside the fork, partly built. wiki:projects/trident/thesis-goals.md:148 lists, among the Baselines: 'original TRIDENT, and a no pre-training + random feature drop control: NAIM's feature drop alone made a purely supervised model robust, so TRIDENT's pre-training gain should be measured against it, not just against no pre-training'. The NAIM page proposes the same baseline (naim-paper.md:331).
cards.api_fit: No pre-training: there is no CLI flag. CONFIGURATION_FLAGS (fork:src/training/config.py:33-36) and the parser (config.py:301-541) have none. EPOCHS_PRE=0 can still be set through datasets/hiperparams/<base>/<variant>.json (config.py:99-127) or an Optuna override. Nothing rejects 0 (types.py:240-277 doesn't validate epochs). The pre-training loop then runs range(0) (pretraining.py:105) and hands the Xavier-initialised model (pretraining.py:71-75) to fine-tuning (finetuning.py:101). One UNTESTED point: the pre-training stage would then build CosineAnnealingLR(T_max=0) (schedulers.py:81-83). Random feature drop: does not exist. Fine-tuning calls preprocess_table(p_base=0.0, fine_tunning=True) (finetuning.py:81-89) and encodes the tables once (finetuning.py:124-126), so supervised training never hides a cell. Building it takes four things. First, an opt-in knob that defaults to off, so classification stays bit-identical (AGENTS.md:6-7). Second, a NAIM-style draw each epoch (Bernoulli(0.5) per row, then c ~ U{1..v-1} observed cells), with the holes written as [NULL] (the inverse of gaps_as_mask, embedder.py:207), not [MASK] as draw_dynamic_mask does. Third, its own RNG stream, as evaluation_mask has (data.py:163-179), so the seeded draw sequence doesn't move. Fourth, a logged param and tag, plus tests.
cards.categorical_support: Native (TRIDENT's embedder, with [NULL] in both column types).
cards.feasible_tables: All 9 tables, all 45 variants.
cards.known_failures: In TRIDENT Table 4 the no-pre-training variant beats TRIDENT at 0% (0.8533 vs 0.8426), although the paper's text says the opposite (trident-paper.md:187). Without its regularizer, NAIM falls to 61.57 AUC at 75% test missingness, against 77.20 with it (naim-paper.md:233-234).
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: TRIDENT Table 4, no-pre-training variant: 0.8533 / 0.8054 / 0.7422 / 0.6683 / 0.5478, mean 0.7234 vs 0.7406 for TRIDENT (trident-paper.md:176-183). TRIDENT was tuned on its test set (trident-paper.md:206).
cards.wrapper_effort: No-pre-training arm: 0.5-1 h (config files and one test that a 0-epoch pre-training runs end to end). Feature-drop arm: 4-6 h of code. Keeping the fork's conventions (flag, tag, untouched vehicle_00nan fixture, typing gate) is most of the cost.
cards.compute_estimate: Inferred from fork:docs/tickets/0003-training-loop-performance.md:74 (electricity: about 1.03 s per fine-tuning epoch on CUDA; 150 fine-tuning epochs by default, types.py:202). About 2.6 min per electricity fit, so roughly 4-7 GPU-h per arm for 675 fits. Full TRIDENT adds 300 pre-training epochs (about 1.76 s each, roughly 9 min per electricity fit), about 20-30 GPU-h for its 675 fits.
cards.gap_exposed: Whether TRIDENT's +1.7 macro-F1 pre-training gain comes from pre-training itself or just from the model seeing holes during training.
cards.rq_or_todo: Step zero (Table 4 replication, thesis-goals.md:148, :152); t11 for what the paper's variants actually were.
cards.reasons: The no-pre-training half is close to free: EPOCHS_PRE=0 through a config file, with one scheduler edge case to test. The feature-drop half is new code that has to respect the fork's bit-identity and RNG-stream rules.
evidence: fork:src/utils.py:18-58 (preprocess_table writes [MASK]; fine-tuning mode masks nothing)

cards.name: Prerequisite: an MNAR variant family (generator + signed-bias metric)
cards.availability: In-fork work, no package needed. Generator sources to reimplement (about 50 lines each, not as dependencies): Muzellec et al. logistic/self-masking/quantile (tracker row muzellec2020missing), probit self-masking with Le Morvan's lambda_j=1/(2 sigma_j), logistic self-masking (Van Ness), MissBench's 9 MNAR generators (github.com/jacobf18/tabular), mdatagen MBOV (Pereira). Avoid importing hyperimpute's simulator: ADR 0016 records that hyperimpute 0.1.17 breaks on scikit-learn 1.9.
cards.api_fit: Today every variant is MCAR. datasets/generate_splits.py:26-49 inject_nans hides exactly round(n*pct) random cells in every feature column, seed 42. An MNAR family needs a sibling injector writing e.g. <table>_20mnar-sm row-aligned with _00nan, so ADR 0004 decision 5 (induced cells = NaN in the variant, observed in _00nan) and the whole scoring path work unchanged. baseline_cache.py hashes the train/test frames (docstring :9-13), so new variants get fresh cache entries for free. Two code changes are unavoidable. (1) A signed mean error per population and per column, because imputation_metrics.py:72-104 has only RMSE, MAE, accuracy and macro-F1, while thesis-goals.md:77 scores the MNAR arm by signed bias. (2) An explicit rule that the headline is the induced population. The masked population is an MCAR eval mask on observed cells (data.py:163-176), so it measures p(x|M=0) reconstruction, not MNAR.
cards.categorical_support: Needs a rule for unordered categories. kr-vs-kp is all 36 categorical, credit-g has 13 of 20 categorical, electricity has 'day' (datasets/categorical_columns/*.txt). Self-masking 'by value' means a per-category propensity there (e.g. one category hidden at p_hi, the rest at p_lo, as in Shades-of-Null's step rule), and the known-sign idea doesn't exist.
cards.feasible_tables: All 9 tables. Calibrate each column's propensity so the expected cell count matches the MCAR variant's round(n*pct), which keeps MCAR vs MNAR at equal rates comparable. If GINA is wanted, leave at least one auxiliary column fully observed, which a MAR-logistic shape does and all-column self-masking does not.
cards.known_failures: Under self-masking at 60-80% few large values survive in training, so every imputer, the bar included, extrapolates. Hard thresholds (not-MIWAE's and GNR's 'above the mean' rule) make the logistic missing model only an approximation (not-miwae-paper.md:106). The fork's 80nan variants already leave ~20% of each column observed.
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: Not applicable (a data-generation step).
cards.wrapper_effort: Roughly 8-14 h: injector plus per-column rate calibration (3-4 h), categorical rule (1-2 h), regeneration and row-alignment checks against _00nan (1-2 h), signed-bias metric in score_cells and per-column output plus a summary key (2-3 h), tests (2 h). The owner first has to choose 1-2 mechanisms (thesis-goals.md:110-120 lists the candidates).
cards.compute_estimate: Generating the variants takes minutes. The real cost is downstream: TRIDENT's decoder plus the bar (mean_mode, knn5/10, hgb, lgbm) and missForest on every new variant, i.e. one more E-series sweep per mechanism x rate (15 fold pairs each), run on gorgona8 as the MLflow store writer.
cards.gap_exposed: This is the dependency for every MNAR-aware card below. Fit on today's MCAR holes, a selection-model imputer is misspecified by construction, so running it on the 21 current variants is only a misspecification control (the not-MIWAE page's Open Question, not-miwae-paper.md:185), not an MNAR baseline. The fork also can't yet report the directional error that defines MNAR damage.
cards.rq_or_todo: RQ1 MNAR arm (thesis-goals.md:77); also feeds RQ2/H2 (informative missingness) and RQ4.
cards.reasons: The code is small and fits the existing row-aligned design. But it needs owner decisions on the mechanism(s) and the categorical rule, a new metric, and a full TRIDENT plus baseline sweep on the new variants before any MNAR-aware imputer means anything.
