cards.name: not-MIWAE (Ipsen, Mattei & Frellsen, ICLR 2021)
cards.availability: Official code is github.com/nbip/notMIWAE: TensorFlow plus TFP (TF1-style graph code, per the Shades-of-Null copy), no license, 17 stars, last push 2021-01-28. A PyTorch port exists: pip `notmiwae-pytorch` 0.1.3 (2025-12-17; requires torch>=1.9, numpy>=1.19), repo github.com/Adam-Ousse/notmiwae_pytorch, MIT, last push 2026-01-12, 1 star, an ENSTA course project. It has MIWAE, not-MIWAE and supervised variants; Gaussian, StudentT and Bernoulli decoders; and missing processes 'selfmasking', 'selfmasking_known_signs', 'linear' and 'nonlinear'. It is compatible in principle with the fork's lock (torch 2.5.1+cu121, numpy 2.4.6, Python >=3.11). HyperImpute has no not-MIWAE: its plugins include plugin_miwae.py (plain MIWAE), and PyPI 0.1.17 (2023-02-28) breaks on scikit-learn 1.9 (ADR 0016). Shades-of-Null's wrapper (github.com/FalaahArifKhan/data-cleaning-stability, MIT) is the TF code pinned to tensorflow~=2.8 / tfp 0.16 / numpy 1.23.5, which has no Python 3.11 wheels, so it can't go in the fork's venv.
cards.api_fit:
Put it in a new module, say src/training/notmiwae_baseline.py, kept apart from imputation_baselines.py so the other families' cache entries survive (the reason lightgbm_baseline.py:11-12 gives). Register it as a 4th _Family('notmiwae', (imputation_baselines, imputation_metrics, notmiwae_baseline), ('torch',), fit_notmiwae_imputers) in baseline_cache.py:65-73, outside the bar like missForest (ADR 0017), and report it as gap_to_notmiwae. Names: notmiwae_agnostic and notmiwae_selfmask_known (thesis-goals asks for both).
- fit(train_frame): build the matrix as KnnImputer does (imputation_baselines.py:129-160). Numericals stay as they are, already scaled. Each categorical becomes a one-hot block over the training vocabulary minus _NOT_A_CLASS ('nan', '[MASK]', '[NULL]', :33-34). s = ~frame.isna() is expanded per block, and the encoder input is zero-filled as in MIWAE.
- impute(frame, hidden): the protocol hands over ONE mask, missing = hidden | frame.isna() (:61-66, used at :93/:164/:296). not-MIWAE's imputation conditions on s (Eq. 15). So on the masked population it would treat the eval-mask cells (MCAR, observed in the frame) as MNAR gaps and shift them toward the self-masked tail. Fix: real = frame.isna(), artificial = hidden & ~real. Zero both in the encoder input, but include the p(s|x) factor only over cells that are not artificial: an MCAR factor is constant and drops out. The port's impute(x, s) takes a single s, so this is a small change to its importance-weight code. Without it, score only the induced population.
- Output: numerical floats in scaled space; categorical argmax mapped to the vocabulary strings; columns in frame order (checked at :365-366).
- RNG: module init, sampling and Adam all use torch's global generator. The fork forbids touching global streams (:40-43; missforest.py seeds its own models; ADR 0016 rejected HyperImpute partly for moving them). So wrap fit/impute in torch.random.fork_rng with a fixed seed, and set deterministic algorithms if it runs on GPU. The cache key already includes the machine.
cards.categorical_support: Not in the port. Its decoders are Gaussian, StudentT and Bernoulli only (notmiwae_pytorch/models/base.py). Bernoulli covers binary columns, and most of kr-vs-kp is two-valued, but credit-g's multi-class columns, kr-vs-kp's 3-valued ones and electricity's 'day' need a softmax head per categorical. The missing model also needs data-space samples of the hidden categories, so use Gumbel-Softmax as the paper did on Yahoo (temperature 0.5, not-miwae-paper.md:88). Shades-of-Null's shortcut ordinal-encodes categories, decodes with a Gaussian and rounds (notmiwae_imputer.py:116-117). That is the 'regress category indices as numbers' approach ADR 0016 rejected for IterativeImputer, so don't copy it. 'Self-masking known sign' has no meaning for unordered categories, so categorical columns get a per-category logistic or the agnostic model.
cards.feasible_tables: All 9 tables and all 21 variants by size; the largest are electricity (~45k x 8), letter (20k x 16) and spambase (4.6k x 57). Tiny MLPs, no GPU required. Risks: spambase, where CACTI saw NaN losses in almost every setting (cacti-paper.md:268), and the 60-80nan variants, where the zero-filled encoder input is mostly zeros. On the current MCAR variants the result is a misspecification control only; the real test needs the MNAR family (card 1).
cards.known_failures: Deep self-masking without the known sign is unstable: Banknote 1.88 +/- 0.85, worse than MIWAE. Deep agnostic on Concrete (2.63) is worse than mean imputation (not-miwae-paper.md:123-135). The authors find that a flexible data model plus a flexible missing model 'can be detrimental'; the linear PPCA variant won on 4 of 6 tables. CACTI: NaN losses on income (MCAR 30%) and on spambase in almost every setting, and CACTI misconfigured it for known self-masking under a non-self-masking MNAR (cacti-paper.md:268, :348). Shades-of-Null: no better than the other leading imputers under step-function MNAR (shades-of-null-paper.md:154). GNR: near random on mask prediction for yeast at high rates (gnr-paper.md:143). The paper uses no early stopping on purpose (not-miwae-paper.md:109), so a fixed iteration count is part of the method.
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: None directly comparable. The paper's own tables are Banknote, Concrete, Red/White wine, Yeast and Breast (not-miwae-paper.md:116-129), none of the 9. CACTI includes Spambase and Letter (cacti-paper.md:212-213) but reports notMIWAE only averaged over 10 tables: R^2 0.29|0.30, RMSE 0.82|0.80 vs mean 0.98|0.95 under its logistic MNAR (cacti-paper.md:236). It also failed on spambase. Shades-of-Null ran it on 'german' (= credit-g, 1,000 rows) under step self-masking with row-wise single-cell injections (shades-of-null-paper.md:100, :121), but results are in figures only and the metric and mechanism don't match impute_score. For a port sanity check, reproduce one UCI row of Table 1 instead: Banknote deep self-masking-known 0.74, PPCA self-masking 0.57 (not-miwae-paper.md:120-125).
cards.wrapper_effort: About 18-28 h. Vendor the MIT port's model files, which avoids depending on a 1-star package (2-3 h). Add a categorical softmax/Gumbel head and categorical missing model (4-6 h). Split the importance weights into real and artificial masks (1-2 h). Encode and decode to the frame contract, reusing KnnImputer's vocabulary code (2-3 h). RNG isolation and determinism (2-3 h). Cache _Family, a backfill script modelled on scripts/backfill_lgbm_baseline.py, and summary gap keys (3-4 h). Reproduce one not-MIWAE Table-1 row on Banknote before trusting the port (2-3 h including runtime). Tests (2-3 h). A linear (PPCA-like) decoder option is about 1 h more and worth having, since it was the paper's best variant.
cards.compute_estimate: Not measured. Basis: a fixed 100k iterations x batch 16 x K=20, 2x128 tanh layers (not-miwae-paper.md:108), so fit cost is roughly independent of table size; at a guessed 1-3 ms/iteration that is ~2-5 min per fit. Folds depend on the seed (data.py:218-221), so 21 variants x 15 fold pairs = 315 fits, x2 missing-model variants = 630 fits, roughly 20-50 device-hours serial. That parallelizes well on gorgona8 because each fit is tiny, and is the same order as ADR 0016's ~40 GPU-hour ReMasker estimate. Imputation scales with test rows x importance samples: the paper's 10k samples on electricity's ~9k test rows needs chunking, or use L=1k. Budget 1.5x for NaN-loss retries. Each MNAR variant later costs 15 x 2 fits.
cards.gap_exposed: Whether TRIDENT's head, which like every hide-and-reconstruct imputer learns p(x|M=0), loses to an explicit selection model on truly MNAR cells, and in which direction (signed bias). It also tests whether the paper's 'flexible data model needs an informative missing model' trade-off applies to a Transformer head. It is meaningless until the MNAR family and the signed-bias metric exist (card 1).
cards.rq_or_todo: RQ1 MNAR arm (thesis-goals.md:77); not-MIWAE page Open Questions (not-miwae-paper.md:185-186).
cards.reasons: A usable MIT PyTorch port exists and maps onto BaselineImputer, but it lacks multi-class categorical heads, needs the two-mask change to avoid biasing the masked population, and needs RNG isolation and a port-validation run. Above all, it is blocked on an MNAR variant family that doesn't exist yet. The TF original and HyperImpute are dead ends for this venv.

cards.name: Delta-adjusted hgb (pattern-mixture sensitivity shift)
cards.availability: No package; a few lines on top of the fork's GradientBoostingImputer. It is the standard pattern-mixture sensitivity analysis: impute under MAR, then shift the imputations of truly missing cells by delta in the assumed MNAR direction.
cards.api_fit: Subclass GradientBoostingImputer the way LightGbmImputer does (lightgbm_baseline.py:30) and override impute. Call super().impute(frame, hidden), then add delta_j * sd_j to numerical fills only where frame.isna() (real gaps), never on hidden & ~isna (eval-mask cells, which are MCAR). sd_j is about 1 because frames are already scaled. For categoricals, add a log-odds offset toward the self-masked category, which needs predict_proba from the column classifiers (the parent keeps them in self._models, :216). Two flavours: an oracle delta from the generator, computed on the training fold from the _00nan sibling and labelled as oracle, and a small fixed grid (0, 0.25, 0.5, 1 sd) for the sensitivity curve. Name them hgb_delta<d>. Register in a new module or family so ADR 0007's cache entries stay valid.
cards.categorical_support: Numerical columns are trivial. Categorical columns need the probability-tilt variant, about 1 h more, and the direction is undefined unless the generator names a 'masked' category.
cards.feasible_tables: All 9 tables and all variants; the cost is hgb's.
cards.known_failures: It is an assumption, not an estimate: delta isn't identifiable from the data. With an oracle delta it is an upper reference, not a competitor, and must be reported as such. A wrong sign makes it worse than hgb.
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: None found.
cards.wrapper_effort: 3-5 h: subclass and real-gap-only shift (1 h), categorical tilt (1-2 h), oracle delta from the generator (1 h), tests (1 h).
cards.compute_estimate: The same as one hgb refit per fold (the cache stores scores, not models): minutes per variant on gorgona8, negligible next to the decoder.
cards.gap_exposed: How much of the bar's (and TRIDENT's) MNAR bias a known-direction shift removes. It gives the scale against which not-MIWAE's 'self-masking known' variant, which is also given the direction, should be judged.
cards.rq_or_todo: RQ1 MNAR arm (sensitivity analysis); RQ4 (assumed-mechanism cost when the assumption is wrong).
cards.reasons: A few hours on an existing class, with no new dependency and no RNG issues, and it reuses hgb's fit. It is only meaningful on MNAR variants (card 1), and it must be labelled a sensitivity analysis rather than an MNAR-aware imputer.

cards.name: Imputation + missing indicator (and mask-aware imputer variant)
cards.availability: Trivial with scikit-learn (SimpleImputer/IterativeImputer add_indicator=True, or concatenating frame.isna()); LightGBM/HGB also handle NaN natively (MIA).
cards.api_fit: The indicator doesn't change the filled value. It is a downstream feature, so it isn't an imputation baseline under BaselineImputer, and impute_score can't see it. Its place is the RQ2 comparator 'conditional imputation + indicator (missForest or condexp + mask) and GBDT native handling (MIA)' (thesis-goals.md:140), and H2's 'fed to the same encoder' (thesis-goals.md:93). The GBDT version needs classification folds, which don't exist in the fork. The same-backbone version needs TRIDENT's embedder to accept a value plus indicator per cell instead of [NULL]. On the imputation side, the closest variant is a mask-aware hgb: give each column's booster explicit indicators of the other columns' real gaps, kept separate from the 20% training-copy hides (_TRAINING_HIDE_RATE, :47-51), which currently share the same NaN branch. That is a 2-4 h subclass overriding _matrix, but hgb and lgbm already route NaN natively, so it adds little.
cards.categorical_support: Native (indicators are binary; median-dummy style 'missing' category for categoricals).
cards.feasible_tables: All 9 tables, once a classification harness exists.
cards.known_failures: Under self-masking an indicator can't remove an imputer's own-column bias, because the target cell's own indicator is always 1. It helps prediction, not imputation. Le Morvan & Varoquaux found that without indicators better imputation hurt XGBoost/SAINT under probit MNAR, and that with them native MIA and missForest+indicator tied for top rank (thesis-goals.md:66, :140).
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: None found for the 9 tables with an indicator arm. Shades-of-Null has no indicator arm (shades-of-null-paper.md:110).
cards.wrapper_effort: GBDT + indicator: 1-2 h once classification folds exist. The fold harness itself is the 'step zero' replication (thesis-goals.md:152) and is not costed here. Same-backbone indicator input for TRIDENT: a day or more (embedder change plus ablation flag). Mask-aware hgb for imputation: 2-4 h.
cards.compute_estimate: GBDT: minutes per variant. TRIDENT-with-indicator: one more classification sweep, the size of the step-zero replication.
cards.gap_exposed: RQ2/H2: whether per-column [NULL] tokens are non-inferior to imputation + indicator on the same backbone under informative missingness. It needs the MNAR (or outcome-dependent) variants of card 1 and classification folds.
cards.rq_or_todo: RQ2/H2 (thesis-goals.md:78, :93, :140); todo t1 (hot.md:18: [NULL] vs missForest/MICE + indicator at 60-80%); step zero.
cards.reasons: The trick itself is trivial, but it belongs to the classification task, which has no folds or results in the fork. As an RQ1 imputation baseline it is a category error, and its mask-aware imputation variant duplicates what hgb/lgbm's native NaN routing already does.

cards.name: Per-column Heckman selection imputer (classical selection model)
cards.availability: A quick search found no maintained Python Heckman imputer and no Heckman model in statsmodels. R has sampleSelection and ssmodels; Stata and EViews have heckman. A Python version means writing a bivariate-normal MLE or two-step with scipy.
cards.api_fit: For each numerical column j: an outcome equation x_j = x_{-j} beta + e, and a selection equation 1[observed_j] = 1[x_{-j} gamma + u > 0] with corr(e, u) = rho. Fill a real gap with E[x_j | x_{-j}, M_j=1] through the inverse Mills ratio. x_{-j} has gaps of its own, so pre-fill the features with the hgb fill (reuse GradientBoostingImputer). Apply the selection correction only to real gaps (frame.isna()), and plain E[x_j | x_{-j}] to eval-mask cells (hidden & ~isna, which are MCAR). Output follows the frame contract. It lives in its own module and cache family.
cards.categorical_support: Numerical only. Binary columns would need a bivariate probit, and multi-class columns have no standard Heckman form, so kr-vs-kp (all categorical) is out and credit-g covers only its 7 numericals.
cards.feasible_tables: Numerical columns of all tables. kr-vs-kp is not feasible. It is weak on credit-g and electricity, where most columns or the key ones are categorical.
cards.known_failures: Without an exclusion restriction (a variable that drives selection but not the value), identification rests on bivariate normality and is fragile. That fits poorly with pure self-masking, where M_j depends on x_j itself, and with skewed lab-like features.
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: None found.
cards.wrapper_effort: 12-20 h: MLE/two-step with scipy plus the Mills correction (5-8 h), feature pre-fill and real/artificial mask split (2-3 h), frame contract and cache family (2-3 h), tests and a simulation check on a known bivariate-normal case (3-5 h).
cards.compute_estimate: Small: one probit plus one regression per column per fold, seconds to minutes per variant on top of the hgb pre-fill.
cards.gap_exposed: A transparent, linear selection-model reference beside not-MIWAE, showing whether the deep model's gain comes from the selection structure or from the nonlinear data model.
cards.rq_or_todo: RQ1 MNAR arm, as an optional classical comparator.
cards.reasons: Nothing to install, but the estimator has to be written and validated. It covers only numerical columns, its identification is fragile under self-masking, and the delta-adjusted hgb card gives most of the cheap insight for less effort.

cards.name: GINA (Ma & Zhang, NeurIPS 2021; 'mnar_pvae')
cards.availability: Code is in microsoft/project-azua, which is ARCHIVED (last push 2022-06-21), MIT, file azua/models/mnar_pvae.py (406 lines). environment.yml pins python 3.8.2, pytorch 1.7.0, numpy 1.21.0, scikit-learn 0.23.2 and pandas 1.1.3. microsoft/causica (its successor, active) is a causal-discovery codebase, and I did not check whether it still carries GINA. Shades-of-Null vendored azua under external_dependencies/ and runs it as 'mnar_pvae' beside TF 2.8, an environment the fork's Python 3.11 can't share. No pip package.
cards.api_fit: mnar_pvae.py:9-15 imports azua's PartialVAE, Encoder, Decoder, MaskNet, Variables and TorchModel. A wrapper means extracting about 6 modules and their Variables/dataset machinery, porting them to torch 2.5 / numpy 2.x, and then the same steps as not-MIWAE: frame-to-Variables encoding with categorical types, real/artificial mask split at impute, torch RNG isolation, and a cache _Family with ('torch',). The fit/impute split is inductive, as Shades-of-Null uses it (fit on train, impute on test).
cards.categorical_support: Native in azua: Variables carry categorical types with a categorical likelihood (categorical_likelihood_coefficient in model_config_mnar_pvae.json).
cards.feasible_tables: The tables are fine by size, but GINA's identifiability premise fails on the fork's data. Its prior net p(z|U) needs always-observed columns; with none it warns 'no fully observed columns, switch to degenerate prior' (mnar_pvae.py:39-44). The fork's injector holes every feature column (generate_splits.py:43-48), so U is empty on all 21 variants, and the baselines never see the label. GINA then becomes a PVAE with a mask net, i.e. a not-MIWAE-like model without the guarantee. It is meaningful only if the MNAR generator leaves auxiliary columns complete, a constraint on card 1's design.
cards.known_failures: Shades-of-Null: no better than the other leading imputers under step self-masking (shades-of-null-paper.md:154, :185; their snapshot line 228). It needs fully observed auxiliary variables (tracker row ma2021identifiable). The default config trains 5000 epochs at batch 100, heavy on electricity and letter.
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: Shades-of-Null ran mnar-pvae on 'german' (= credit-g), but results are in figures only, with row-wise injections and an F1/RMSE metric that isn't impute_score. Its own paper uses synthetic self-masking and recommender data (tracker row). None found on the other 8 tables.
cards.wrapper_effort: About 30-45 h: extract and port azua modules to torch 2.5/numpy 2.x (12-20 h, given the 2020-era pins), Variables adapter for the fork's frames (4-6 h), the not-MIWAE wrapper items (mask split, RNG, cache, backfill: 8-12 h), and a validation run against Shades-of-Null or a synthetic case (4-6 h).
cards.compute_estimate: Not measured. 315 fold-pair fits at the default 5000 epochs is far heavier than not-MIWAE on the large tables (letter 16k and electricity ~36k training rows per fold), so it needs a reduced epoch budget. Expect at least ReMasker-scale device-hours (ADR 0016: ~40 GPU-h).
cards.gap_exposed: An identifiable MNAR imputer vs TRIDENT. But on the fork's data it can't be identifiable unless the generator keeps auxiliary columns complete, so today it would only duplicate not-MIWAE.
cards.rq_or_todo: RQ1 MNAR arm (thesis-goals.md:77); tracker ma2021identifiable (relevance 3).
cards.reasons: Archived 2020-era code tangled with a framework, a port to the fork's stack, and its defining feature (auxiliary U) is absent by construction in every current and planned all-column MNAR variant. Run not-MIWAE first, and revisit GINA only if card 1's generator keeps a fully observed subset.

The Python core hard-codes device 'cuda:0' throughout (e.g. inst/NIMIWAE.py:50-56, :183, :227), so it won't run on CPU without edits. cards.name: summary.py bar and external-baseline machinery (EXTERNAL_BASELINES, _best_baselines, _paired_gaps)
cards.availability: In the fork: src/training/summary.py:83-185, called by summarize_cross_validation (summary.py:51-80) and logged by tracking._log_summary_metrics (src/training/tracking.py:412-437). No install needed.
cards.api_fit: Store-side, no report code. Any fold key matching impute/<population>/baseline/<name>/impute_score (regex at summary.py:85) is picked up automatically. A name not in OUTSIDE_THE_BAR (summary.py:88-92) JOINS the bar: it can become best_baseline/<pop>, gets copied under baseline/best, and moves gap_to_best_baseline (summary.py:95-148). Adding the name to EXTERNAL_BASELINES (summary.py:88) keeps it out of the bar and gives it gap_to_<name> and gap_to_<name>_pct with 7 stats (summary.py:151-163). For the name to appear at all, the baseline needs a _Family in src/training/baseline_cache.py:64-74 with a fit function returning BaselineImputer objects (imputation_baselines.py:54). score_baselines then emits baseline/<imputer.name>/<metric> (imputation_baselines.py:374), and decoding.py:188-214 puts that into the fold metrics and raw_fold_metrics.csv on LIVE runs.

cards.known_failures: (1) The gap's model key is f"{population}/impute_score" (summary.py:174), the run's HEADLINE. On E34 and E35, the cells every report treats as today's default, the headline is H (loss checkpoint), and K lives at impute/induced/induced_checkpoint/impute_score. Verified read-only on sync/incoming.db: gap_to_missforest = H - missForest on 63/63 E35 parents. Example kr-vs-kp_80nan seed 42: H 1.0121, K 0.9716, the store's gap_to_best_baseline is +0.0121 (H vs mean_mode 1.0) while K is below the bar. (2) The gap is per run (5 folds, one seed). There is no 3-seed verdict in the store.

cards.name: backfill_lgbm_baseline.py as the template for backfilling MICE/HyperImpute onto existing runs
cards.availability: In the fork: scripts/backfill_lgbm_baseline.py (387 lines), built on scripts/backfill_baseline_imputers.py (670 lines). Dry run by default, --apply writes the store, and only the server (gorgona8) may write it.
cards.api_fit: Copy-edit: NEW_BASELINES = ("lgbm",) is hardcoded (backfill_lgbm_baseline.py:69); the family list comes from baseline_cache.FAMILIES. It recomputes every baseline's 5 fold values through the live cache (plan_lgbm receives them as `folds`, :105-119). It checks mean_mode against the logged numbers to 1e-9 (:70-79), then writes: (a) 7 CV stats on the parent at step 0, (b) the fold value on the 2 diagnostic children only (best_fold/worst_fold, tracking.py:229-257, summary.py:344-360), (c) gap_to_<external> via plan_external_gaps (:197-226), and it re-mirrors (:229-247). It never rewrites metrics/raw_fold_metrics.csv or cv_summary.json (docstring :28).
cards.categorical_support: Inherits the live scorer: categorical metrics wherever the table has categorical columns.
cards.feasible_tables: All 887 imputation parents ADR 0017 touched (commit e333fb7), including E34 and E35 (63 each). E38 carries lgbm live in 48/63 CSVs; the 6 pendigits/letter ALL cells were backfilled.
cards.known_failures: (1) plan_external_gaps takes the model's mean from cv/test/{population}/impute_score/mean (:211), so on E34/E35 it writes an H-based gap, not K. (2) After the backfill, 3 of every 5 fold values of the new baseline exist nowhere persistent, so no report can pool 15 fold pairs. Store check: 0/63 E35 CSVs and 0/63 E34 CSVs have lgbm or missforest columns. (3) Review finding 7 (docs/reviews/2026-10-07-code-review-last-two-weeks.md:205-218, untracked): the ADR 0007 backfill's plan_run with checked=None refuses every run carrying baseline/best once CURRENT_BASELINES grows (backfill_baseline_imputers.py:111), and writes the parent before the children. (4) KNN and hgb last digits differ by machine, so only mean_mode is checked (:70-74).
cards.published_numbers_on_same_tables: Fork's own: ADR 0017's backfill moved the bar on 658 of 887 parents and corrected missForest on 102 runs by up to 0.0056 (commit e333fb7 message).
cards.wrapper_effort: 3-5 h. Copy the script with NEW_BASELINES set to the new names, add a K-based gap (model key impute/<pop>/induced_checkpoint/impute_score where present), and write a sidecar per-fold artifact, e.g. metrics/backfilled_fold_metrics.csv holding the in-memory `folds` dict. All the data is already in hand at plan time (:105-119). Without the sidecar, the 15-pair verdict needs either the sidecar or a fresh run.
cards.compute_estimate: Dominated by the new imputer's fits: 5 folds x 2 populations per parent, for 126 parents (E34+E35) or 189 with E38. The reporting overhead is small.
cards.gap_exposed: Backfilled baselines are invisible to every CSV-reading report. The pooled 15-pair CI can be rebuilt exactly from three parents' per-seed gap (mean, std, n=5), with SS = sum[(n-1)s^2 + n(m-M)^2]. This works only if that per-seed gap is the K gap, so the K-based gap in this card is the minimum fix.

cards.reasons: The skeleton is proven on 887 runs, but three changes are needed beyond a rename: the K-gap, the per-fold sidecar and the finding-7 ordering and refusal fix. It also runs on the server only.
